title: Measles deaths may have been 'fabricated,' RFK Jr claims after coroner raises questions
summary: RFK Jr. alleged Pennsylvania's two measles-associated deaths may have been "fabricated" as a dispute with Gov. Josh Shapiro over the outbreak intensifies.
story: CNN's Dana Bash sparred with HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. over vaccine efficacy amid rising measles cases in the U.S. on "State of the Union" Sunday.
Days after Pennsylvania health officials reported two measles deaths, a public dispute has emerged about whether other factors played a role in the fatalities.
The Pennsylvania Department of Health (DOH) confirmed the two "measles-associated" deaths on Tuesday, noting that both individuals were unvaccinated.
These were the state’s first measles-related deaths in 35 years, according to the release.
FORMER CDC ADVISOR SAYS DECLINE IN KINDERGARTEN VACCINATIONS NOTHING TO WORRY ABOUT: 'KEEP CALM AND CARRY ON'

That confirmation came after the county coroner — physician Stephen Diamantoni — said the newborn died shortly after birth from a lacerated spleen and had tested positive for measles acquired before birth, according to The Philadelphia Inquirer.
Days after Pennsylvania health officials reported two measles deaths, a public dispute has emerged about whether other factors played a role in the fatalities. (iStock)
Diamantoni’s office was still investigating the newborn’s death, and the coroner said he was not aware of the other reported death, Axios reported.
The Pennsylvania Department of Health stated that not all deaths are referred to a coroner under state law.

The DOH says it uses the term "measles-associated" when laboratory or epidemiologic evidence of measles is present, even if a coroner or medical certifier does not identify measles as the immediate cause of death.
The Pennsylvania Department of Health (DOH) confirmed two "measles-associated" deaths on Tuesday, noting that both individuals were unvaccinated. (iStock)
Measles can affect the spleen, potentially causing enlargement and, in rare cases, rupture, according to Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News senior medical analyst.
Pregnant women, newborns and young infants can face a higher risk of serious measles complications, the doctor noted.
Infants who are too young to receive the MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine can be especially vulnerable.
COMMON VACCINE LINKED TO 24% LOWER DEMENTIA RISK IN OLDER ADULTS
HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has questioned whether Pennsylvania officials provided sufficient information to substantiate the two measles-associated deaths.

In a Wednesday post on X, after the coroner’s comments were made public, Kennedy alleged that Pennsylvania had not given the CDC relevant information and suggested the deaths could have been "fabricated."
Measles can affect the spleen, potentially causing enlargement and, in rare cases, rupture, according to Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News senior medical analyst. (iStock)

"The announcement appears to have been premature, and the deaths may even have been altogether fabricated by one of the Governor's hopeful staffers," he wrote. "The Lancaster County Coroner says that it has no record of any measles deaths."
RFK also accused Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro and his office of "fearmongering, misinformation, finger-pointing and the weaponization of infectious disease fears for political gain."
"The Lancaster County Coroner says that it has no record of any measles deaths."
Meanwhile, at a Tuesday press conference, Shapiro said the deaths showed the "real-life consequences" of misinformation about the measles vaccine.
In a subsequent X post, the governor claimed Kennedy had "stoked confusion amongst parents and others — and the result has been less protection from measles and more cases."
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

In response to Kennedy’s comments, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention also spoke on X about the debate, expressing appreciation for RFK’s efforts to "clarify conflicting information" about the cause of the two reported deaths.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"CDC is working to determine what actually occurred," the agency wrote. "These discrepancies raise important questions, particularly because the Governor’s Office has not provided CDC with information relevant to the outbreak and has declined our offers of assistance."
"Under President Trump’s and Secretary Kennedy’s leadership, CDC will follow the facts and tell the American people the truth."
HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has questioned whether Pennsylvania officials provided sufficient information to substantiate the two measles-associated deaths. (REUTERS/Elizabeth Frantz)
Pennsylvania Health Secretary Dr. Debra Bogen disputed the CDC’s account, saying the two deaths were reported to the agency’s measles response team early Tuesday morning.

In an X post from the Pennsylvania Department of Health account, Bogen said she had reviewed the case investigations and that state epidemiologists had thoroughly investigated both deaths. She confirmed that both individuals tested positive for measles.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Meanwhile, Lancaster County Commissioner Josh Parsons said he did not believe there was enough evidence to confirm the two deaths were caused by measles, citing information he said he received from the county coroner’s office, according to Local21 News.
What does ‘measles-associated’ mean?
Siegel noted that measles weakens the immune system and increases the risk of pneumonia, which can stem from measles itself or from a secondary bacterial infection.

When a patient has both measles and another immediate cause of death, several considerations come into play when infectious disease specialists are determining whether the virus was a contributing factor. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)
"If the impact of measles on the immune system or stress on other major organs as a result of the disease leads to death, that would be a measles-associated death," he told Fox News Digital.

When a patient has both measles and another immediate cause of death, several considerations come into play when infectious disease specialists are determining whether the virus was a contributing factor.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"It has to do with whether the immediate cause of death is from measles itself, as in measles pneumonia, or due to damage to the immune system and secondary infections or other diseases that result," Siegel said.
Lancaster County is at the center of Pennsylvania’s current measles outbreak. As of Friday, the state had reported 424 confirmed cases and 73 hospitalizations.
Fox News Digital reached out to RFK Jr. and other officials requesting comment.

title: Common vaccine linked to 24% lower dementia risk in older adults
summary: A Brown University study found Shingrix reduced dementia risk by 24% over four years, building on prior research linking the shingles vaccine to brain health.
story: Neurologist Dr. Ajeet Sodhi breaks down research linking the shingles vaccine to a reduced risk of dementia, while stressing that the findings show an association, not proof that the vaccine treats dementia.
A recent study led by researchers at Brown University appears to strengthen the link between shingles vaccination and a reduced risk of dementia diagnoses in older adults.

The study, published in The Annals of Internal Medicine, evaluated electronic health records and Medicare claims for more than 509,926 U.S. adults 66 and older who were admitted to skilled nursing facilities.

Individuals who received at least one dose of the recombinant shingles vaccine, commercially known as Shingrix, experienced a 24% relative reduction in dementia risk over a four-year period compared to people who did not receive the shot, the researchers found.
ALZHEIMER'S RISK MAY BE 35% LOWER WITH COMMON MENOPAUSE TREATMENT, STUDY FINDS
However, the findings show an association and do not prove that the vaccine directly prevents dementia, the researchers noted.

Dr. Ajeet Sodhi, a clinical neurologist and neuro-interventionalist in Orlando, Florida, noted that while the finding is "remarkable," it builds upon a growing foundation of scientific literature rather than standing alone.
Independent neurologist Dr. Ajeet Sodhi noted that these findings align with recent studies suggesting a link between shingles vaccines and slower cognitive decline. (iStock)

"This is maybe the third or fourth study, and they all came to the same conclusion," Sodhi, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital. "It seems that by giving patients the shingles vaccine called Shingrix, in the next couple of years, we see a clinically significant decline in the development of dementia."

Researchers have proposed several possible explanations for the association, including the vaccine's role in preventing shingles and its potential complications. The virus has also been linked to vascular events such as stroke, which can contribute to vascular dementia.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Sodhi noted that recent medical literature continues to support larger cardiovascular benefits as well.

"In addition to the study that we're talking about today, there was a study published just this week that showed the shingles vaccine results in a clinically significant reduction in the incidence of both cardiovascular disease and cerebrovascular disease," he told Fox News Digital.
"So that's heart attacks and strokes."
"The common theme in all of this is the sooner you seek evaluation, the better it is for the treatment."
The neurologist emphasized that while the data shows a strong correlation, the vaccine is not currently classified as a direct therapeutic treatment for cognitive decline.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"It's not at this time considered a treatment," he noted. "This association is ... very, very suggestive, but we can't say one-to-one it proves that this treats dementia. And this finding, honestly, is kind of like icing on the cake."
Beyond potential brain health benefits, the primary purpose of the FDA-approved vaccine is to prevent painful shingles reactivations and long-term nerve damage. (iStock)
Shingles is caused by the varicella-zoster virus, the same virus responsible for chickenpox, according to Mayo Clinic.
After a person recovers from chickenpox, the virus lies dormant in nerve tissue near the brain and spinal cord, where it can reactivate decades later as a painful rash with fluid-filled blisters.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
The primary function of the vaccine remains the prevention of the severe nerve pain and rash caused by shingles reactivation.
Shingles can lead to severe complications, including post-herpetic neuralgia, a debilitating condition causing long-term nerve pain that persists after the rash clears, according to Cleveland Clinic.
The FDA recommends the two-dose Shingrix series for adults 50 and older, with specialists emphasizing that early medical assessment is critical for managing cognitive health. (iStock)

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends two doses of Shingrix for adults 50 and older, as well as adults 19 and older who are or will be immunocompromised. The vaccine is FDA-approved to prevent shingles and related complications — not to prevent or treat dementia.
The study received funding from GSK, the maker of Shingrix; the authors stated that the company had no role in the study’s design, analysis or publication.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
For individuals concerned about memory loss or family medical history, experts recommend consulting a doctor early.

"The common theme in all of this is the sooner you seek evaluation, the better it is for the treatment," Sodhi advised. "The treatment is more likely to work the earlier you are in the onset of the disease."

title: Smithsonian showdown intensifies as Trump administration issues a stark new warning
summary: The Smithsonian Institution faces threats beyond its $1 billion federal funding as Trump administration claims evidence of antidiscrimination violations.
story: Fox News host Laura Ingraham accuses the Smithsonian of promoting a divisive 'activist agenda' and 'restorative history' that negatively frames America. She highlights National Museum of American History director Anthea Hartig's testimony regarding the museum's educational materials and controversial exhibits, including an alleged 'fetish attire' display and the exclusion of pro-life history. Ingraham questions the use of taxpayer funds for such programs.

The Trump administration says it has uncovered evidence that the Smithsonian Institution violated federal nondiscrimination laws and is threatening to withdraw support from its museums unless it corrects course, according to a letter recently made public by the Department of the Interior.

"The administration has recently uncovered evidence that the Smithsonian leadership's institutional culture may have resulted in significant violations of Federal antidiscrimination law, including creating a hostile work environment and engaging in practices that classify individuals and allocate opportunities, funding and other benefits on the basis of race, ethnicity and other protected characteristics," a letter sent jointly to the Smithsonian by the DOI and White House reads.

Specific evidence of illegal activity on the part of the Smithsonian was not included in the letter, and the DOI did not provide further information when reached for comment. A recent Fox News Digital investigation found that many leading figures at the Smithsonian, including those involved in hiring, have been strong proponents of diversity, equity and inclusion — something the Trump administration has previously framed as racially discriminatory.
TRUMP’S SMITHSONIAN CLASH EXPOSES STRIKING PATTERN AMONG MUSEUM CURATORS
President Donald Trump blasted the Smithsonian on Truth Social Tuesday for being "OUT OF CONTROL" and "woke." (Getty Images)

Conservative political leaders, led by President Donald Trump, have accused the Smithsonian of allowing progressive ideology to shape its presentation of American history. An executive order signed in 2025 directed officials to remove what it called "improper ideology," from the museum.

"The Executive Order signed by the President of the United States clearly states ‘the Secretary of the Interior, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, the Administrator of General Services, and the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy shall identify and utilize any and all available authorities to promote the policy of this order and to restore trust in the Smithsonian Institution," a DOI spokesperson told Fox News Digital.
TRUMP TARGETS BIDEN-ERA BILLION-DOLLAR SMITHSONIAN BUDGETS AMID ANTI-'WOKE' PUSH
Liberals have framed criticism of the Smithsonian as a partisan attempt to influence the presentation of history. (Alex Wroblewski/AFP via Getty Images)
Liberals, meanwhile, have framed conservative criticism of the Smithsonian as a partisan attempt to influence the public presentation of history.

Unless the Smithsonian remedies the issues outlined in the DOI’s recent letter, as well as the general bias which conservatives allege exists at the institution, the administration says it will consider pulling support from it. The threats this time around, however, differ from the ongoing fight over the roughly $1 billion a year in federal funding the Smithsonian receives.
SMITHSONIAN'S TAXPAYER FUNDS FACE CHOPPING BLOCK AS GOP DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY FOR 'WOKE' HISTORY
The Smithsonian's National Museum of American History was called out for being "ideologically captured" and presenting woke revisionist history. (Kevin Carter)

"Those executive departments and agencies cannot in good conscience continue to support the Smithsonian under current leadership by, for example, loaning artifacts for exhibits, enabling procurement processes and making discretionary grants," the letter reads.

While the letter does not provide specific changes that the administration would like to see from the Smithsonian, it does note that an "appropriate response" from the organization "must likewise address executive leadership and institutional ideology."

That wording could be significant as the institution operates independently but is overseen by board members appointed by congressional resolutions that the president must sign into law. By October, there will be four openings on the institution’s board of regents, a fact the administration may leverage to increase its influence over the Smithsonian.

"Very few Americans want the Smithsonian National Museum of American History to be used, in the words of its director, as a ‘prime tool of social justice’ and as an instrument of ideological activism and advocacy,"  Vince Haley, the director of the White House's Domestic Policy Council told Fox News Digital when asked about the letter. "Unfortunately, the Saving America’s Story report demonstrates, using the statements of Museum leadership and the interpretive guidelines adopted by the Museum, that this is exactly what the Smithsonian’s flagship museum has become."

"During this 250th anniversary year of our heroic founding, the least our citizens are owed is an honest and inspiring account of American history. It should begin by telling the story of our Founding Fathers — who they were, what they did, and what they built. It is our hope and expectation that the Smithsonian will eventually rise once again to that noble obligation — to tell America’s story for our children, the world and future generations of Americans," he added.
WATCH: SMITHSONIAN HISTORY MUSEUM DIRECTOR STUMBLES OVER BASIC QUESTIONS ON SEX: ‘I’M NOT SURE’

Anthea Hartig, director of the Smithsonian Institute's National Museum of American History, testifies during a House subcommittee hearing titled "Rewriting American History: Examining the Smithsonian's Efforts to Reshape the Past," on July 21, 2026. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

DOI requests that representatives from the Smithsonian meet with administration officials "at [their] earliest convenience" to discuss the alleged bias and civil rights violations present at the institution.

"The museum does not take sides in America’s political debates. We preserve and document the evidence of American life in all of its breadth, so that the public can encounter the past and draw their own conclusions," National Museum of American History’s director Anthea Hartig said at a July congressional hearing.
The Smithsonian declined to comment on the letter when reached by Fox News Digital on Thursday.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Recent reporting has found that the museum’s leadership and many of its curators have backgrounds in liberal advocacy or Democratic politics. In addition to exhibits at the National Museum of American History, which the Trump administration characterized as demonizing America, even the Smithsonian-run National Zoo is inundated with information about DEI and gender equity.

title: White House rips ‘activist’ Biden judge who upended Trump birthright citizenship order
summary: A Biden-appointed judge blocked President Donald Trump's birthright citizenship executive order, calling it "almost certainly unconstitutional."
story: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin discusses a federal judge blocking President Donald Trump’s birthright citizenship executive order, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul’s response to ICE crackdowns and a recent emergency landing.

A Biden-appointed judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's latest executive order seeking to limit birthright citizenship, setting up another high-profile legal battle over the scope of the 14th Amendment.

In a 35-page ruling, U.S. District Judge Deborah Boardman issued a preliminary injunction against the Oval Office's Aug. 6 executive order, which was issued a month after the Supreme Court affirmed birthright citizenship in its ruling in Barbara v. Trump. The injunction is the first to halt Trump's revised birthright citizenship order since the Supreme Court upheld birthright citizenship in June.
Boardman previously blocked Trump's original birthright citizenship executive order before the Supreme Court weighed in on the issue.

Trump's order sought to limit birthright citizenship for children whose parents are deemed alien enemies, including members of designated Foreign Terrorist Organizations, and children whose foreign parents paid a surrogate in the U.S. to give birth, among several other restrictions. The executive order prompted Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA) to file a lawsuit against the Trump administration.
TRUMP BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP FIGHT COMES ROARING BACK WITH ‘INVADERS’ PLAY AFTER KAVANAUGH ROADMAP
Demonstrators gather outside the Supreme Court in Washington, D.C., in support of birthright citizenship, May 15, 2025. (Kent Nishimura/Bloomberg via Getty)

"The 2026 Executive Order is almost certainly unconstitutional as applied to the certified class for the simple reason that the Supreme Court in Barbara already decided that the children in the class are citizens at birth," Boardman wrote in her ruling. "This Court must, once again, preliminarily enjoin enforcement of the President’s most recent attempt to strip the right to citizenship from them."
The White House rejected Boardman's ruling as the work of an "activist judge appointed by Biden attempting to thwart President Trump’s commonsense agenda."
"The birthright citizenship executive order is consistent with the holdings and analysis set forth by the Supreme Court," Lauren Bis, White House spokeswoman, said in a statement.

In a 5-4 decision on the constitutional question of birthright citizenship, the high court held that children born in the United States to parents who are unlawfully or temporarily present in the country are "citizens at birth" under the 14th Amendment in Barbara v. Trump.
TRUMP’S TOUGHER ROUND-TWO BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP STRATEGY HINGES ON KEY LEGAL DISTINCTION, EXPERTS SAY
Demonstrators hold up an anti-Trump sign outside the U.S. Supreme Court in Washington, D.C., on June 27, 2025. (Alex Wroblewski/AFP via Getty Images)

While the Supreme Court has acknowledged exceptions to birthright citizenship, such as children of foreign diplomats or children born during an enemy's hostile occupation of U.S. soil, Boardman rejected Trump's latest executive order targeting children born to alleged alien enemies. She agreed with the plaintiffs' concerns over the Trump administration's "broad view of who qualifies as an enemy." The plaintiffs alleged that the Trump administration had "sometimes resting its conclusions on false or speculative allegations, or even tenuous markers like tattoos or family affiliations."

Boardman pointed to two plaintiffs — Andrea, who fled an area of Mexico where a designated cartel operates and whose child’s father has a relative in the group, and Monica, a Venezuelan woman who fears her family could be wrongly linked to Tren de Aragua.
TRUMP SIGNS EXECUTIVE ORDERS TARGETING BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP, BIRTH TOURISM AFTER SUPREME COURT SETBACK

President Donald Trump speaks during a press conference at the White House, on June 27, 2025, following a Supreme Court ruling that limits the application of birthright citizenship. (Mehmet Eser/Middle East Images via AFP)

"Children whose parents may 'rightly or wrongfully' be deemed by the government to be alien enemies face a credible threat of "being denied or stripped of their birthright citizenship ... even though they do not fall within a recognized exception to birthright citizenship," Boardman wrote.

However, Abhi Kambli, a former Justice Department official, said Boardman was speculating on how the Trump administration could incorrectly bar someone from citizenship based upon being part of a foreign terrorist organization.

"Legally, where that falls short is that it's a facial challenge to the entire executive order," Kambli told Fox News Digital. "So, in legal terms, when something's a facial challenge, you have to demonstrate that it's unlawful in all of its applications, and not just the edge, the borderline cases."

"She didn't want to wade into the territory of whether that fits as an exception generally within Trump v. Barbara, but she said that based on how they've interpreted it in the past and in terms of what happened with Tren de Aragua and other organizations, she bought into plaintiff speculation that maybe they'll get it wrong this time, and then that'll affect their kids, and then that's why it should get barred," Kambli continued.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
Boardman used the First Circuit's language to find that denying citizenship under the new executive order would cause irreparable harm — one of the requirements for issuing a preliminary injunction.

"The loss of birthright citizenship — even if temporary and later restored at the conclusion of litigation has cascading effects’ that will ‘very likely leave permanent scars’ on the child and their family," the ruling stated.
Monica celebrated the preliminary injunction.

"During my pregnancy, I felt so much anxiety over the fact that my child could be born stateless," Monica, said in a statement. "For now, my child and children like mine are protected and guaranteed U.S. citizenship. But I know this isn’t over. The threat to birthright citizenship is still out there. I’ll keep fighting for permanent protection for my child, and for every child born in this country."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"When it comes to attacking birthright citizenship, the Trump administration has lost before this court, lost before the Supreme Court, and lost again today," Shana Khader, legal director at We Are CASA, said in a statement. "The White House must recognize it will not succeed in stripping children of their right to citizenship, evading binding court decisions or placing the president’s anti-immigrant agenda above the Constitution. We are very proud to continue this fight alongside the families who have endured more than a year of fear and uncertainty and still refuse to surrender their children’s constitutional rights."
Elaine Mallon is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business covering national politics.

title: Vance reveals who's behind his recent weight loss in first White House press briefing since July
summary: The vice president credited Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s diet of high protein and sauerkraut for his weight loss during his first press briefing since the departure of Karoline Leavitt.
story: Vice President JD Vance addresses a question from Fox News senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy about his weight loss over the last few months while conducting a press briefing Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026.

While conducting the first official White House press briefing since July 23, when he led it, and the first since former press secretary Karoline Leavitt's departure last month, Vice President JD Vance addressed a myriad of topics Thursday, including the Iran war, oil and gas prices, inflation and Republican messaging ahead of the midterms.
There were also a few light moments during the briefing, such as when Fox News senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy asked Vance about his weight loss over the past few months.

"So, when you're the vice president of the United States and one of the first questions at a press conference in the White House is how much weight you've lost, you must have gotten very fat," quipped Vance, who's no stranger to the media grilling session, the third he's helmed.
RUBIO REJECTS RFK'S 'CRAZY' DIET, JOKES POP-TARTS ARE 'ONE OF THE GREAT AMERICAN INNOVATIONS'
Vice President JD Vance speaks during a press briefing at the White House in Washington, D.C., Thursday. (AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein)
Vance said advice from Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is what got him on his weight loss journey since Lent in February.
He said he called Kennedy and told him he was thinking of giving up sugar.

"Bobby Kennedy says, 'No, no, no, no, I've got something that's way better than that and way more intense.' And basically ... I eat a lot of high protein stuff, and I eat a lot of sauerkraut. And let's just say that if that was Fat Tuesday, Fat Wednesday never came," Vance said.
"So, my advice to you is that if you want to lose weight, call Bobby Kennedy. And if you want to enjoy what you eat, do not call Bobby Kennedy."
Vice President JD Vance said his weight loss journey began around Lent this year. (Alex Wong/Getty Images, File)
POPULAR DIET SLASHES LIVER FAT BY 67% WHILE REVERSING PREDIABETES IN SOME PEOPLE
In a January interview with USA Today's "The Excerpt" podcast, Kennedy said he was on a "carnivore diet."
People on carnivore diets eat only animal products, such as meat, dairy and eggs, but the program is frowned upon by some who embrace plant-based foods like vegetables, fruits, grains and legumes.

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., speaks during a meeting to sign an executive order about vaccines Aug. 10 in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, D.C. (Jacquelyn Martin/AP Photo)

"That may not be right for other people, but I lost 40% of my visceral fat within a month," Vance said on the podcast, referring to the fat that surrounds internal organs and is linked to higher risks of cardiovascular disease.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
He also claimed he had improved his mental clarity, adding that he lost 20 pounds in 20 days after switching to the diet. He acknowledged some of the benefits could be due to the placebo effect.

title: Vance jokes about rubbing elbows with former president at Ground Zero: ‘Intense intellectual conversations’
summary: JD Vance says he's "looking forward" to seeing Joe Biden at the World Trade Center 9/11 ceremony alongside former presidents and Rudy Giuliani.
story: Vice President JD Vance said Thursday he is "looking forward" to "hanging out" with former Vice President Joe Biden while the two of them attend a ceremony at Ground Zero on the 25th anniversary of 9/11.
Vice President JD Vance said Thursday he is "looking forward" to meeting with former President Joe Biden while in New York City next week for the 25th anniversary of 9/11.

"I'm really looking forward to hanging out with Joe Biden. I'm sure that we'll have many, many intense intellectual conversations and, you know, it'll be great. We'll have a great time with Joe Biden and the other presidents," Vance said while hosting the first White House press briefing after former press secretary Karoline Leavitt exited in August.

Vice President JD Vance will travel to Ground Zero on 9/11, joining former Presidents Barack Obama, George W. Bush and Bill Clinton and former first ladies Hillary Clinton and Laura Bush for a remembrance ceremony.
TRUMP CONFIRMS PENTAGON PLANS FOR 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF 9/11 ATTACKS, DISPUTES REPORT ON GROUND ZERO ABSENCE
Vice President JD Vance speaks during a news briefing at the White House on Sept. 3, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
The last known time Vance and Biden were in the same room was at President Donald Trump’s inauguration on Jan. 20, 2025, in the U.S. Capitol Rotunda.

"We just decided as a team that I would go to New York for 9/11 and the president would stay here in D.C., of course, to commemorate what happened at the Pentagon, because that was a critical part of the tragedy of 9/11 as well," said Vance.
FIRST ON FOX: TRUMP’S 9/11 TRIBUTE TO FEATURE MASSIVE PIECE OF GROUND ZERO HISTORY AT WHITE HOUSE

Former President Joe Biden and former first lady Jill Biden board a helicopter outside the U.S. Capitol following President Donald Trump's inauguration on Jan. 20, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Getty Images)

Trump is expected to attend a ceremony at the Pentagon, and other administration officials will represent the White House in Shanksville, Pennsylvania — marking all three locations targeted or affected by the attacks. Vance said during the press conference that there was no indication Trump was staying in the nation's capital due to security concerns in New York City.
9/11 IS BECOMING HISTORY. MY GENERATION MUST MAKE SURE AMERICA NEVER FORGETS

Donald Trump attends the annual 9/11 commemoration ceremony at the National 9/11 Memorial and Museum on Sept. 11, 2024, in New York City alongside Vice President Kamala Harris, President Joe Biden, former New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg and then-Sen. JD Vance, R-Ohio. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

"I will say that as much as it's tragic and it was a terrible day, I am looking forward to it because it's such an amazing honor to be able to get to go to New York and to share in that moment," said Vance.
Vance said it is especially meaningful for parents to show their children the names of those who were killed, recalling that he did so with his own family during the 2024 campaign.

"It's one of the most amazing experiences of my life, and I encourage every American, particularly the people who are young enough to not really remember that day, just to tune in for a couple of hours and see what it meant," Vance added.

Vance said the tragic day brings a "sense of commonality and common purpose" for Americans to unite.

title: White House gives classic arcade games a MAGA makeover in new online launch
summary: The White House launched a gaming website with MAGA remakes of Snake, Flappy Bird, Duck Hunt and Tetris designed to highlight Trump's second-term wins.
story: The White House is rolling out a new website Thursday featuring classic arcade-style games with a MAGA twist. (Credit: The White House)
FIRST ON FOX: The White House is rolling out a new website Thursday that will feature classic arcade-style games with a MAGA twist.
A promotional video for the site obtained by Fox News Digital shows MAGA remakes of old favorites, including Snake, Flappy Bird, Duck Hunt and a couple of originals. Each one is uniquely Trumpian.

The MAGA version of Snake, for example, features border czar Tom Homan leading a line of illegal aliens in orange jumpsuits while he chases others on the grid. In another game, reminiscent of Duck Hunt, the user employs a net to catch gold bars and money, illustrative of putting money into a Trump Account. The Washington Monument is depicted in the background of that game.
The MAGA version of Snake from arcade.gov features Tom Homan capturing illegal aliens. (The White House)
SEN DAVE MCCORMICK: TRUMP ACCOUNTS GIVE ALL AMERICANS A STAKE IN PROSPERITY
The White House says the new site is a fun way to highlight Trump's successes in his second term.

"This administration is laser focused on ways to innovate and tell the story of the president’s many accomplishments in a way that resonates with every American," a White House official told Fox News Digital.
BIG TECH JOINS FORCES WITH TRUMP ADMIN TO UNLEASH PATRIOTIC BIRTHDAY PUSH INTO HOMES NATIONWIDE
Visitors to the new site can also play the administration's version of Flappy Bird, flying a bald eagle through obstacles on the National Mall.
The MAGA version of Tetris on arcade.gov, where players can build a wall on the southern border. (The White House)

In the fourth game, the user is a boxer, punching unhealthy foods like candy away. The game features a graphic with the words "Seed Oils" with a red line through it in a nod to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and his Make America Healthy Again initiative.
AOC SAYS MAHA ADVOCATES' FIGHT 'ISN'T PARTISAN' AS SHE BLASTS HEALTHCARE SYSTEM FOR FUELING 'A TON OF ANXIETY'
Another resembles Tetris, set at the southern border, where the user's goal is to build a wall to stop the flow of illegal immigration into the U.S.
The site is also a jab at Democrat policies and what the White House describes as the political left's "dark" vision for the future of the country.

"The president continues to rack up victory after victory on behalf of the American public, while opponents of his agenda are defending their record of raising taxes and empowering criminal illegal aliens," the official told Fox News Digital.
"This is an effort to further contrast between a culture of fun and winning and the dark socialist vision Democrats have for America."
President Donald Trump speaks in the Oval Office Aug. 14, 2025 in Washington, D.C. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Millions of foreigners have left the United States, either by voluntary self-deportation or by being arrested and removed, during Trump's second term.
Those numbers are on the rise. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) recently broke its own monthly record for illegal alien arrests, topping 50,000 in July.

Parents are eligible to open Trump Accounts for their children this year, in which the federal government automatically deposits $1,000. Family members and friends can contribute up to $5,000 per year to a child's account, which will appreciate in value until the child turns 18. The program will continue next year.
Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Dem Senate hopeful vows to unleash Alaska oil — but her record tells a different story
summary: Mary Peltola touts Alaska oil production in her Senate bid, but in Washington, D.C., she urged colleagues to vote against her own ANWR drilling bill.
story: Alaska Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola turned down an endorsement from former Vice President Kamala Harris as her campaign asserts that her focus is on the people of Alaska.

A Democrat eyeing a return to Congress in a crucial battleground state has pitched a policy platform geared toward expanded oil production, but she once turned her back on the issue while in Washington, D.C.

Former Rep. Mary Peltola is running to unseat Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, in a contest that could define the balance of power in the upper chamber. National Democrats have Alaska in their sights as a viable pickup opportunity in their quest to flip the Senate, but Peltola is running away from some of their greener energy policies to push for expanded oil production.
Earlier this month, she unveiled her "Making Energy Affordable for Alaskans" plan that zeros in on oil and gas development in her state, which is one of the top crude oil producers in the country.
DAN SULLIVAN ACCUSES SAME-NAME CHALLENGER OF TRYING TO 'RIG' ALASKA SENATE RACE

Former Rep. Mary Peltola is pushing for more oil and gas production in Alaska, but when she was in Congress, she urged Democrats to kill her own bill that would've done just that.  (Nathan Posner/Anadolu via Getty Images)

"Alaska has always been a leader in energy production, and as an independent voice for Alaskans, I will always stand up to anyone to invest in Alaska energy production so that we can create good-paying jobs and lower energy costs," Peltola said in a statement introducing the plan.

"As D.C. price hikes create an energy catastrophe for Alaskans, we can’t afford more delays, political gridlock, or one-size-fits-all rules from the Lower 48 that leave Alaskans without solutions," she continued.

In 2023, she did have an opportunity to do just that. During her time in the House, Peltola and Rep. Pete Stauber, R-Minn., introduced the Alaska’s Right to Produce Act, legislation that would have reversed several Biden-era rules and regulations that limited or canceled oil and gas leases in Alaska.

When it came time to vote on the bill, which would have required the reinstatement of canceled drilling leases in the non-wilderness Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (ANWR) and overturned lease restrictions in the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska (NPR-A), she urged her colleagues to vote against it.
DEM SENATE NOMINEE CHANGES TUNE ON ICE AFTER VOWING NOT 'ONE MORE DIME' FOR AGENCY
Peltola, in a letter sent to House Democrats first reported by the Alaska Story, called on her colleagues to vote against her own bill out of fear that it would go too far.

"I am the Democratic co-lead for this bill and voted for it in committee. However, this legislation has a significant unintended consequence that could adversely affect Indigenous communities and the Arctic Ocean environment," Peltola wrote.

"The bill’s intent is to allow Alaska to maintain onshore oil and gas, but a provision within it would nullify the Northern Bering Sea Climate Resilience Area, potentially harming these communities and the environment," she continued.

"I support oil and gas development. Alaska needs energy, and we have a wealth of resources that could be developed. However, the unintended consequences of this bill are too significant to allow it to pass."
SENATE REPUBLICAN PUSHES OVERHAUL TO CUT RED TAPE AND SPEED UP AMERICAN ENERGY PROJECTS
Newly introduced Senate candidate Dan Sullivan, left, pictured alongside Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, right. (Sullivan for U.S. Senate; Brandon Bell-Pool/Getty Images)

A key reason that Peltola urged her colleagues to vote against the bill was because of a provision tucked away in the legislation that would have effectively pitted the oil and gas industry against the fishing industry in Alaska — two key economic drivers in the state. Peltola later introduced a clean version of the bill that didn't include that provision.

She also scored wins for energy production in the state during her time in Washington, including getting the Biden administration to reverse course on ConocoPhillips' Willow Project, an $8 billion oil drilling project in the National Petroleum Reserve.

"Mary’s record is clear: She will always put Alaska first, and no one from the Lower 48 will ever tell her how to vote or how to think," a spokesperson for her campaign told Fox News Digital. "That’s why she took on her own party to secure the Willow project after years of delays and why she introduced legislation to open the ANWR and NPR-A for oil development, with input from Alaska’s fishermen."

"Mary supports creating good-paying oil and gas jobs, securing America’s energy independence, defending the right of Alaskans to develop our own land, and bringing down the cost of energy for Alaska families – and that’s what she will fight for in the Senate," they continued.
The bill did ultimately pass in the Republican-controlled House but died on the vine in the Senate, which was run by then-Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y.

And Schumer heavily recruited Peltola to mount a bid against Sullivan, giving her the full weight of the Democratic establishment in her race against Sullivan, who is seeking a third term in the upper chamber.
Though she’s portrayed herself as someone willing to buck the party, Sullivan’s campaign argued her record and list of endorsements showed the opposite.

"As a Congresswoman, Mary Peltola turned her back on Alaska time and time again," Nate Adams, a spokesperson for Sullivan’s campaign, told Fox News Digital. "Peltola says whatever she needs to say to get elected, then goes to Washington and does whatever Chuck Schumer, AOC, and D.C. Democrats demand of her, even when it directly hurts the Alaskans she’s supposed to represent."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Peltola’s shameless ability to say one thing to Alaskans and do the exact opposite in Congress might be why she cashed out and became a lobbyist when Alaskans fired her in 2024," he continued.

Their battle isn’t as cut-and-dried as other contests on the Senate map, however. Dan J. Sullivan, a retired schoolteacher also running as a Republican, is on the ticket — a situation that Alaska Republicans tried to thwart through legal action over concerns that his candidacy was meant to confuse Alaska voters in their ranked-choice voting system.
Voters will choose among Peltola, both Sullivans and Gerald Heikes, another Republican eying the seat, in November.
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Vance refuses to put a clock on Iran conflict as key question keeps US forces engaged
summary: JD Vance refuses to set an artificial timeline on Iran, citing Strait of Hormuz attacks and a full pivot from diplomacy to military pressure.
story: Vice President JD Vance said Thursday he will not put an "artificial timeline" on the war with Iran as tension continues to escalate in the Middle East following recent U.S. airstrikes.
Vice President JD Vance said Thursday he will not put an "artificial timeline" on the war with Iran, warning that the conflict will continue on as long as Iran keeps shooting at ships.

"You're asking me a question like, when will the Iranians stop shooting at ships? I think the reality is, I don't know the answer to that question. You would have to ask the Iranians, when will the Iranians shooting at ships stop having an effect on world energy markets? And the answer is it has less effect day by day," Vance said while hosting the first White House press briefing after former press secretary Karoline Leavitt exited in August.

Vance said the U.S. will not depend on the Iranians "behaving responsibly" or "negotiating in good faith," pointing to recent attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The Trump administration has taken negotiations off the table after June’s failed Memorandum of Understanding agreement and has pivoted back to economic and military pressure.
IRAN DEAL CLOCK HITS ZERO AS TRUMP DEMANDS ‘WHITE FLAG’ WITH NEW PRESSURE CAMPAIGN LOOMING
Vice President JD Vance speaks during a press briefing at the White House in Washington, D.C., on Sept. 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein)

"What we're going to do is use the tools that we have at our disposal to ensure that the American people, one, never have to deal with the threat of an Iranian nuclear program and, two, the world, energy markets are properly supplied," said Vance.
The conflict began on Feb. 28, 2026, when the U.S. and its partners launched Operation Epic Fury, striking targets across Iran at President Trump’s direction.

U.S. Central Command said Tuesday that American forces completed a wave of strikes against targets inside Iran, including air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets, mine-laying capabilities and communications sites.
US EMBASSIES IN MIDDLE EAST WARN AMERICANS OF 'UNFORESEEN ESCALATION' AS LATEST STRIKES HIT IRAN
A gas flare on an oil production platform is seen alongside an Iranian flag in the Gulf on July 25, 2005. (Reuters/Raheb Homavandi/File)
Vance said the conflict with Iran is not a war, citing that there are no active shootings but "places where this is flared up" and acknowledged major combat operations that lasted under six weeks.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas in southern Iran on Aug. 10, 2026. (Atta Kenare/AFP via Getty Images)

"Since then, we destroyed, of course, their nuclear facilities with Midnight Hammer. With Epic Fury, we destroyed their defense industrial base for producing weapons and also a lot of their conventional military and then we made it harder for them to rebuild that nuclear program," Vance added.
Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

title: Lawmakers press DHS in letter over Chinese forced labor allegations, flag popular Labubu dolls
summary: The House CCP Committee demands a DHS briefing on enforcing the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act as Chinese goods from slave labor reach U.S. markets.
story: Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., the ranking member on the House Select Subcommittee on the CCP, explains the committee's decision to request further information from DHS about its enforcement against China's alleged use of slave labor in manufacturing.

FIRST ON FOX — The House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is requesting a briefing from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) on the agency's implementation of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA), a law designed to combat the import of Chinese goods made with slave labor, according to a letter shared exclusively with Fox News Digital.

The UFLPA, passed in 2021, directed DHS' Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force to develop a strategy for quelling the importation of goods into the United States that are "manufactured wholly or in part with forced labor in the People's Republic of China."

Human rights groups began shining a spotlight on the alleged oppression and forced labor the CCP was imposing on Uyghurs, a Muslim ethnic minority in China's Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR), a sparsely populated Chinese territory in the country's far west.
MOTHER RECOUNTS HORRORS OF BRUTAL CHINESE DETENTION CAMP WHERE INFANT SON DIED

"The Uyghurs are being politically persecuted in Xinjiang, China. They are being forced to give up their religion. They're being forced to assimilate into Chinese culture. And many of them are being forced to do labor, to work for low wages or no wages and long hours," Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., the ranking member on the House Select Committee on Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview.

Protesters demonstrate outside the Chinese embassy in London against the alleged oppression of Muslim minorities in Xinjiang, demanding that Beijing dismantle its internment camps and respect basic religious freedom. (Krisztian Elek/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)
Khanna argued that enforcement of the UFLPA is not just a moral issue, but one of economic and national security for Americans.
KHANNA DEMANDS ANSWERS FROM CCP-LINKED COMPANY ACCUSED OF UNDERCUTTING US MANUFACTURERS

"This is a human rights violation, but the broader problem also for Americans is that they're making steel, they're making aluminum, they're making textiles, and then they're dumping it into the U.S. market. How could U.S. Steel or Cleveland Cliffs or our aluminum manufacturers compete with slave labor? Of course we can't. So what our letter does is it says that we need more of these companies that are using forced Uyghur labor to be designated by the Department of Homeland Security," Khanna continued.

The bipartisan letter, addressed to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asks the agency to address 10 concerns the committee has, including what work DHS and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) are doing to update the list of companies and entities on the UFLPA Entity List.
GSA FINDS CHINA-MADE TECH LABELED 'MADE IN USA' IN FEDERAL PROCUREMENT PROGRAM, ORDERS SWEEPING REVIEW
DHS added an additional 43 companies to the list in July, an action that Khanna applauded.

"I think the administration may have gotten wind that we were doing this letter and that precipitated action. You know, for a year, they hadn't done anything. Now, I give them some credit for having 44 of these companies on the list. But hopefully, once the letter goes out, we'll see more action," he said.
CHINA’S ROUTING OF BIDEN IN CHIP WAR WITH US CREATED A COMMUNIST TECH GIANT

The committee's letter highlights concerns that products produced by companies on the list and that are coming from the XUAR are still making their way to U.S. customers. Those products, the letter alleges, cover supply chains ranging from steel and aluminum to silicon-carbon materials critical to technology production.
The letter highlights a New York Times report that suggests the cotton contained in popular "Labubu" dolls comes from slave labor.
THE CCP’S NEW ‘UNITY’ LAW TURNS CHINA’S REPRESSION INTO A GLOBAL THREAT
Labubu x World Cup co-branded Designer Toys authorized by FIFA for the first time in the Pop Mart store in Shanghai, China on July 13, 2026. (CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images)

"A lot of the textiles are coming, they come from China, are coming from Uyghurs. It's one of the easiest places to force people into labor, and that's why we included it, because of the reports that Uyghurs are involved in textile production," Khanna added.
Khanna also explained how China circumvents the import bans by outsourcing manufacturing.
TRUMP JUST EXPANDED HIS TARIFF PLAYBOOK WITH A POWERFUL TRADE WEAPON NO PRESIDENT HAS EVER USED

"It's very challenging. I mean, obviously, conventionally, China has been evading some of the tariffs and protections by having their companies open up in Malaysia or Vietnam. Here, of course, you've got actual slave labor. And so what we're saying is identify these products back to the source. And if the source of the textile or steel or aluminum is forced Uyghur labor, then that should not be in the United States," he told Fox News Digital.

Ultimately, Khanna stressed, the problem of forced labor in China is a bipartisan issue, a statement seemingly reflected by the fact that the letter was signed by eight lawmakers, four Republicans and four Democrats.
CHINESE ESPIONAGE STEALS $600 BILLION FROM US FIRMS YEARLY. IT’S TIME FOR GOVERNMENT TO ACT
Rep. Ro Khanna speaks during the National Action Network National Convention in New York City on April 8, 2026. (Brendan McDermid/Reuters)

"This is about fair trade and human rights. Americans aren't concerned about fair competition. If China had laborers that were being paid a fair wage and they were making something and we wanted to buy from them and they weren't dumping, and if China were buying from us, that would be fine. But what can't happen is them using slave labor, undercutting our market and our companies, and then not allowing our companies to sell to them. That's just not fair," he told Fox News Digital.
"Most Americans believe in trade, but they want fair trade and they don't want to be competing with slave labor," Khanna concluded.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Fox News Digital contacted the Department of Homeland Security, Customs and Border Protection, the Chinese Embassy in the U.S., and Pop Mart, the maker of Labubu, for further comment.

title: Feds bust LGBT podcaster, former Christian reality TV star for alleged threats to kill Trump
summary: Benjamin Azariah Southworth allegedly posted videos calling for President Donald Trump's assassination and targeted the family of his attorney.
story: Rep. Randy Fine spoke with Fox News Digital after a man was arrested by federal authorities for allegedly vowing death on Fine and President Donald Trump.
A prominent LGBT podcaster who formerly hosted a Christian reality television show was arrested by federal agents in Los Angeles Thursday for allegedly threatening to kill President Donald Trump.

Benjamin Azariah Southworth, 40, was indicted by a grand jury on federal charges for cyberstalking, making harassing interstate calls and threatening to kill President Trump, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California Bill Essayli announced on X.
He said that Southworth led a harassment campaign against the family of one of Trump's personal attorneys.
Federal agents arrest Benjamin Azariah Southworth on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, for allegedly threatening to kill President Donald Trump. (United States Attorney Bill Essayli)
TRUMP'S DECADE OF ASSASSINATION THREATS RUNS FROM BUTLER SHOOTING TO LATEST GOLF CLUB BREACH

"Southworth is charged with posting videos calling for President Trump’s assassination, then targeted the family of the President’s personal attorney by publishing their home address and phone numbers, and leaving voicemails threatening 'justice comes to your door," Essayli said.
The act of publicly revealing personal information of public officials and celebrities without their consent is known as "doxxing" and is usually done with the intent to harass, shame or cause harm.

"Threats against the President of the United States are federal crimes. We will not tolerate threats of political violence in the United States. My office will prosecute anyone who crosses that line to the fullest extent of the law," the U.S. attorney wrote in a statement on X.
On Southworth's website "Holy Menace," which is still live at time of publication, the podcaster sells $5 stickers that say "Kill Trump."

While being taken into custody by agents, Southworth yelled, "Donald Trump is a pedophile. The country has fallen!" according to the New York Post, which had a photographer present at the time of his arrest.
Court documents obtained by the publication allegedly state that on April 7, 2026, Southworth posted a video on his Instagram account that contained a series of threats against Trump.
Benjamin Azariah Southworth attends The Queerties on March 12, 2024, in Hollywood, Calif. (Chelsea Guglielmino/Getty Images)
"I have been vocal in calling for the execution of Donald Trump," he allegedly said. "This government is illegitimate and out of control. It’s time for course correction. Kill Donald Trump."
The documents allegedly include a myriad of other examples of Southworth making threatening comments against the president, but the papers are not publicly available.
MAN INDICTED FOR ALLEGEDLY POSTING GRUESOME DEATH THREATS AGAINST KRISTI NOEM, PAM BONDI ON SOCIAL MEDIA
"Anyone who engages in or endorses political violence or assassination culture must be condemned in the harshest terms possible," White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told Fox News Digital.
"They should also immediately seek psychiatric help to treat their severe and debilitating case of Trump Derangement Syndrome that has warped their brains and made them sick in the head."

In the late 2000s, Southworth hosted the Christian reality TV show "The Remix," which aired on some of the largest Christian networks in the country, including National Religious Broadcasters TV. The show featured Christian musicians and bands.
Flamy Grant, Benjamin Azariah Southworth, Daniel Franzese and Grace Baldridge, aka Semler, attend The Queerties on March 12, 2024, in Hollywood, Calif. (Chelsea Guglielmino/Getty Images)
In 2008, Southworth came out as gay. He was subsequently the opening act for gay Christian singer Ray Boltz on the singer's nationwide tour in 2010.

In 2020, he started a podcast called "Yass, Jesus!'" which is described as "an interfaith and sexuality affirming comedy podcast that believes you don't have to pick between gay and God." He cohosts the show with "Mean Girls" actor Daniel Franzese, who is also gay.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Southworth could not be immediately reached for comment.
Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Blue state governor candidate claims he ‘met Satan in person’ in resurfaced podcast episode
summary: Colorado Republican Victor Marx claimed on his podcast he "met Satan in person" while praying for a girl at a high-security Texas youth prison.
story: Colorado GOP gubernatorial nominee and Marine veteran Victor Marx told Fox News Digital he sees socialism gaining ground in Colorado and nationally, warning it is
Colorado's Republican gubernatorial nominee claimed in a resurfaced podcast episode that he "met Satan in person" through another person.

Talking Points Memo first reported that Colorado GOP gubernatorial nominee Victor Marx, a Marine veteran and Christian ministry leader, claimed in a 2020 episode of his podcast, "I’ve met the devil" and "I’ve met Satan in person, through a person."

According to Marx’s account on his podcast, the encounter occurred when he was praying for a girl in a high-security youth prison in Texas. He said, "This girl started manifesting a demon" and emphasized, "it was so real that all the other locked up girls, all the other gang members, man, they all kind of huddled in a corner."

Marx described the encounter as "horrible," saying, "This demon… just really manifested pretty nasty." He said that when he asked the demon its name, it responded, "I am Satan." He added, "If you think I’m joking, I’m not."
TRUMP-APPOINTED JUDGE BLOCKS BLUE STATE'S CRACKDOWN ON ICE DETENTION CENTER

Republican candidate for governor Victor Marx poses in the studio used to record his podcast at his campaign headquarters on June 4, 2026, in Colorado Springs, Colo. (Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images)
Though Marx described the little girl as "just adorable," he said he could tell "she had a demon in her."

"All of a sudden, this demon goes, ‘I guess you’re going to say I’m possessed.’ And I just — I just started laughing," said Marx, adding, "I was like, ‘I don’t think I have to. It’s kind of obvious.’ I mean, really, that’s — I just snickered, which makes the devil mad."
Marx is the founder of All Things Possible Ministries, a Christian ministry whose website says it is devoted to "setting captives free spiritually, emotionally and physically."
'GHOST TOWN?' COLORADO BUSINESS LEADERS WEIGH ALL OPTIONS AS DSA GAINS GROUND
From left, state Rep. Scott Bottoms, Victor Marx and state Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer square off during a GOP gubernatorial debate in Denver, Colorado on June 2, 2026. (AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post)

He is pitching himself and his running mate, retired Marine Col. George Markert, as political outsiders, arguing that they have the discipline and accountability needed to take on the movement.
SOCIALISTS RISING IN COLORADO? SEND IN THE MARINES, GOP NOMINEE SAYS
Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser, a Democratic candidate for governor, attends a caucus event at George Washington High School in Denver on March 3, 2026. (AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post)

He has built his long-shot campaign around public safety, social conservatism and the cost of living. The campaign comes as the Democratic Party's left flank scored a series of primary wins nationally, including in Colorado, where democratic socialist Melat Kiros upset longtime incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette.

title: Mamdani gives influencers special access as Signal use raises records-law questions
summary: Zohran Mamdani's City Hall uses a Signal group chat to feed talking points to 200-plus social media influencers, raising record-keeping concerns.
story: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is giving special access to a network of more than 200 social media influencers who take City Hall talking points and videos to promote municipal programs online to residents, according to a new report.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is giving special access to a network of approximately 200 social media influencers who take City Hall talking points and videos to promote municipal programs online to residents, according to a new report.
The report, by the Columbia Journalism Review, highlights that the online personalities get their talking points through an encrypted Signal group text, called "NYC Creators Announcements."

Signal offers a disappearing-messages feature that can automatically delete messages after a set period of time if enabled. It is unclear whether that feature is active in the Mamdani administration’s group, raising questions about compliance with city record-keeping laws.

Questioned by reporters whether the use of Signal possibly breaks city laws, Mamdani said, "My administration will always strive to fully comply with all legal requirements, including those that relate to the preservation of city records."
THIS IS WHAT MAMDANI JUST BANNED FOR NEW YORK CITY STUDENTS IN ELEMENTARY AND MIDDLE SCHOOLS
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks to reporters during a news conference in New York on Feb. 17, 2026. (AP Photo/Seth Wenig)
"If there are any departures from what is legally required, my administration will look into it immediately and take corrective action," Mamdani added on Wednesday.

The use of Signal for government communications made major headlines last year, when then-Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth came under fire after sensitive, real-time details about U.S. military strikes were shared in a Signal group that included a journalist.

The Columbia Journalism Review report also said influencers are not paid by the city for participating in the group or for their coverage, although some receive payments from marketing and advertising firms with contracts from city agencies for work on specific messaging campaigns. The municipal programs promoted include voting, healthcare, immigration and tenants’ rights, participatory budgeting and composting.
HEAD HERE FOR THE LATEST FOX NEWS REPORTING ON NYC MAYOR ZOHRAN MAMDANI
NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani delivers his inauguration address, on Jan. 1, 2026, outside City Hall in New York City. (Fox News / Pool)
City employees told researchers the payments to influencers for their work ranged from $5,000 to $20,000 per campaign, according to the report.

The Signal group was formed out of Creators4Zohran, a group that supported Mamdani’s 2025 mayoral campaign. Mamdani rocked the political world by winning election as the first socialist mayor of the nation's most populous city.

The group chat is steered by Emilia Rowland, the New York City director of new media and cultural communications. Rowland and her staff push out daily updates, talking points, and clips that the influencers can use in their posts.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

New York City Democratic mayoral candidate Zohran Mamdani celebrates as he takes the stage at his election night watch party at the Brooklyn Paramount on November 4, 2025, in the Brooklyn borough of New York City. Mamdani defeated Independent candidate Andrew Cuomo and Republican candidate Curtis Sliwa in the closely watched election for New York City mayor. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty)
The chat operates like a traditional press list used by communications teams to send updates and information to reporters.
Cities are increasingly using influencers to promote municipal services, policies and to engage the public more directly than through traditional media.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"New Yorkers get their news in a wide variety of ways, and it is our responsibility to ensure that we communicate information from city government directly to the people of the city, whether that means to all of you, to TV, to radio, to social media, to content creators and so on and so forth," Mamdani emphasized.
Fox News Digital reached out to City Hall but didn't receive a response at the time this report was published.
Paul Steinhauser covers the national campaign trail from coast to coast for Fox News

title: GOP Sen Thom Tillis urges Trump to replace Pete Hegseth, blasts Pentagon leadership
summary: Sen. Tillis called for President Trump to replace War Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing the Pentagon chief of "creating a leadership void at the top of our military ranks."
story: Fox News chief national security correspondent Jennifer Griffin discusses Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitting his resignation to President Donald Trump, the reported tensions within Pentagon leadership, and the latest developments in the escalating U.S.-Iran conflict, including what the shake-up could mean for America's military strategy and national security on 'America Reports.'

Outgoing Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., called for President Donald Trump to replace War Secretary Pete Hegseth, slamming the Pentagon leader following the news that Army Secretary Dan Driscoll was resigning.
"I urge the President to find a new leader at the Pentagon who will retain and empower our military talent rather than diminish it," Tillis declared in a fiery Wednesday post on X.

Tillis praised Driscoll in the post — and apparently referring to ex-Army chief of staff Gen. Randy George (ret.), the senator declared, "He and General George began a transformative period of innovation in how we array our forces and equip our Soldiers. He challenged our legacy approach to manning and procurement. Most of all, he cared deeply about the men and women in our Army formations and quickly earned their respect."
But Tillis excoriated Hegseth.

"If we had a @SecWar who maintained the same priorities and forward-thinking, he would be fighting to retain talented leaders like Dan and the many flag officers he has forced into retirement. Instead, he is creating a leadership void at the top of our military ranks," the senator wrote.
ARMY CHIEF OF STAFF ORDERED TO RETIRE IMMEDIATELY AS HEGSETH CONTINUES PENTAGON SHAKEUP
Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., talks with reporters in the U.S. Capitol on Friday, August 7, 2026. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

"I served on Senate Armed Services for 8 years and as chair or ranking member of the Personnel and Readiness subcommittee. I have never witnessed more inept management of the brave men and women who serve our country. He is intimidated by competence and retreats to ginning up culture wars instead of soberly attending to the vital work of our national defense and the health and well-being of our fighting force," the lawmaker declared.

Tillis, who announced last year that he would not seek re-election, told Politico Magazine earlier this year that he would "love to see Pete Hegseth fired because he's incompetent and doing a horrible job."
The War Department declined to provide comment on Thursday.

White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said in a statement to Fox News Digital, "After Joe Biden’s Pentagon prioritized DEI and woke ideology, President Trump and Secretary Hegseth quickly reversed course and restored a Department of War that is focused on readiness, lethality, and supporting our warfighters. The President has complete trust in Secretary Hegseth, who is doing an incredible job leading the Pentagon. The results of Operations Midnight Hammer, Absolute Resolve, Southern Spear, and Epic Fury speak for themselves."
TRUMP'S ARMY SECRETARY HUNT TAKES SHAPE AS INSIDERS FLOAT POTENTIAL PICKS

Then-U.S. Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll, War Secretary Pete Hegseth and President Donald Trump attend a dignified transfer at Dover Air Force Base for military casualties of the war with Iran on July 22, 2026, in Dover, Del. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
Driscoll, in a Tuesday statement issued on the official Secretary of the Army X account, noted that Wednesday would be his final full day in the position.

"As a third-generation Army veteran, it has been the honor of a lifetime to serve as the Secretary of the Army under President Trump and Secretary Hegseth. Tomorrow is my last full day in the role," Driscoll said in the statement.

"I had the privilege of working with them to modernize and accelerate how the Army mans, trains, and equips the most lethal fighting force on the face of the earth. We could not have made the progress we did without the support of Secretary Hegseth. I am forever grateful to President Trump for the opportunity to once again serve my country," he noted.
ARMY SECRETARY DAN DRISCOLL SUBMITS RESIGNATION TO TRUMP
President Donald Trump and War Secretary Pete Hegseth listen to questions from the press during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David in Maryland, on July 31, 2026. (Aaron Schwartz / AFP via Getty Images)
