A source familiar with Driscoll's resignation indicated to Fox News that "Driscoll brought up concerns with the administration surrounding Army transformation and readiness and Hegseth's blocking those efforts specifically by firing the Generals who were responsible."
Fox News Digital's Sophia Compton and Fox News' Jennifer Griffin and Liz Friden contributed to this report.
Alex Nitzberg is a writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Illegal alien's ‘inexcusable’ crime sparks interstate clash between GOP sen, Dem gov: ‘You should be ashamed’
summary: Bernie Moreno says an illegal immigrant granted a Connecticut driver's license killed a 29-year-old Ohioan in a vehicular manslaughter case.
story: The father of a 7-year-old girl left permanently disabled after an illegal immigrant driving an 18-wheeler slammed into the vehicle she was traveling in tore into Democratic lawmakers during a Capitol Hill hearing Tuesday, rejecting their expressions of sympathy and accusing them of failing families like his.

Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, is demanding answers from Connecticut’s Democratic Gov. Ned Lamont after an Ohio man was killed in a car crash by an illegal immigrant who Moreno says was granted a driver's license by the blue state governor's policy.

"My office has learned that an illegal alien granted a drivers license by the state of Connecticut killed a 29 year old Ohioan in a reckless driving accident," Moreno posted on X on Tuesday night. "While one death alone is an inexcusable tragedy, Connecticut has granted over 60,000 such licenses to illegal aliens, putting countless Americans at risk on the roads. This insanity has to stop."

Moreno also called on Lamont to "immediately apologize for his state’s role in this tragedy while also account for exactly how many illegals have been given Connecticut drivers' licenses and whether or not they have used them to vote in U.S. elections."

Washington Guillermo Naula-Ochoa, 34, was driving a 2024 Ram 3500 westbound in Fulton County, Ohio on Aug. 29 when he allegedly failed to yield at a stop sign and pulled into the intersection of State Route 66, according to the Ohio State Highway Patrol.
THREE-TIME DEPORTED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH KILLING NORTH CAROLINA GIRL, 6, AFTER RUNNING STOP SIGN

Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, criticized Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont after he says an illegal immigrant charged in a fatal Ohio crash had been issued a Connecticut driver's license. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images; Corrections Center of Northwest Ohio; Tyler Russell/Connecticut Public via Getty Images)

Naula-Ochoa’s car then struck a 1993 GMC Suburban driven by Austin J. Karr Grimes, 29, of Fayette, Ohio. Grimes lost control, went partially off the roadway and overturned. He suffered fatal injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.

Two passengers in Naula-Ochoa’s truck were uninjured, while two passengers in Grimes’ vehicle suffered minor injuries. Naula-Ochoa was charged with vehicular manslaughter and failing to yield at a stop sign.

Naula-Ochoa’s booking record at the Corrections Center of Northwest Ohio (CCNO) shows an immigration detainer lodged against him by federal authorities. Additionally, Naula-Ochoa is listed as "homeless."

"The safest way to arrest and remove criminal illegal aliens from our streets is by lodging arrest detainers," a DHS spokesperson told Fox News Digital, confirming the ICE detainer was placed on Naula-Ochoa, an Ecuadoran national. "7 of the top 10 safest cities in the United States cooperate with ICE. Our message is clear: if you come into our country illegally and break our laws, we will find you, we will arrest you, and we will deport you."
Moreno’s X post was accompanied by a letter sent to Lamont tying him to the Connecticut program that allows for illegal immigrants to be licensed on the road.
ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SUSPECT CHARGED IN CRASH THAT KILLED POLICE OFFICER AND HIS GIRLFRIEND
Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont Jr. (Tyler Russell/Getty Images)

"Despite his lack of legal status, Connecticut issued him a driver’s license," Moreno wrote. "Horrifyingly, Connecticut not only permits illegal aliens to receive a driver’s license, but encourages it, all while Americans pay the ultimate price."

Moreno’s letter criticized Connecticut’s drive-only license program, backed by Lamont, which allows certain individuals who cannot establish legal presence in the United States or provide a Social Security number to obtain a license for driving purposes.

"Quite simply, your policies are killing my constituents," Moreno wrote to Lamont, adding, "You should be ashamed of this policy and its dangerous consequences, yet your support for illegal aliens knows no bounds."

Moreno also criticized Lamont’s 2024 proposal to remove the "drive-only" marking from the licenses, arguing that the change would make them difficult to distinguish from other non-REAL ID licenses. Lamont’s office said at the time that the change was intended to protect Connecticut residents from discrimination in other states.

Moreno asked Lamont to provide the number of drive-only licenses issued to people who are unlawfully present, how many recipients have committed crimes, how many registered or voted, and how much the program has cost taxpayers.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, issued a public statement Sunday calling on his former son-in-law, Rep. Max Miller, to resign from Congress. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

"I strongly suggest that you consider joining the vast majority of states that have adopted this common-sense requirement before another American citizen becomes the victim of vehicular manslaughter or is gravely injured by an illegal alien," Moreno wrote.
In a statement to Fox News Digital, Lamont said his "heart goes out to the family and friends of Austin J. Karr Grimes, and to all families who lose a loved one to a motor vehicle accident.."

"Drivers must be held accountable for violating traffic laws, especially when it causes a tragic loss of life," Lamont said. "States including Connecticut offer drive-only licenses to undocumented residents to help ensure all drivers are trained, tested, and know the rules of the road. This reduces hit-and-run accidents and brings more drivers into the insurance system who might otherwise be driving uninsured. Undocumented residents in many states already need to drive for work, school, and daily life; it’s safer for everyone when that driving happens within a regulated system."

Moreno responded on X on Thursday, saying, "The answer to the presence of illegal aliens is NOT to 'train them' and allow them on our roads to wreak havoc. The answer is to DEPORT them! Of course, Democrat politicians know this, but need a crop of dependent and obedient voters to keep them in power."

The question of illegal immigrants driving on American roads has become a Trump administration priority, with federal officials arguing that state-issued licenses can make it harder to identify and locate people in the country illegally.

The Justice Department sued New York in 2025 over its "Green Light Law," which allows illegal immigrants to obtain driver’s licenses while restricting the state from sharing DMV information with federal immigration authorities. The administration has also expanded ICE enforcement against criminal illegal immigrants, arguing that local arrests should trigger federal immigration action.

Mehek Cooke, a GOP strategist and attorney in Ohio, told Fox News Digital, "What is especially infuriating is that Connecticut Democrats get to congratulate themselves for being compassionate, while an Ohio family is left grieving the loss of 29-year-old Austin Karr Grimes."

"Connecticut made the policy choice, but Americans hundreds of miles away paid the price." Cooke said. "There is nothing compassionate about a policy that puts the interests of illegal immigrants ahead of the lives and safety of American citizens."
Andrew Mark Miller is a reporter at Fox News. Find him on Twitter @andymarkmiller and email tips to AndrewMark.Miller@Fox.com.

title: Dem Senate nominee changes tune on ICE after vowing not 'one more dime' for agency
summary: Hallie Shoffner said she'd defund ICE at an Arkansas event, but Tom Cotton's attack ads prompted her to redefine her immigration enforcement stance.
story: Arkansas Democratic Senate nominee Hallie Shoffner vowed to defund ICE in June but has since backtracked after opponent Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., attacked her over it. (Credit: Young Adult Committee of the Sebastian County NAAC, June 7)
A Democrat running for the Senate in ruby-red Arkansas once called to defund immigration enforcement, but has since changed her tune.

Arkansas Senate Democratic nominee Hallie Shoffner, a farmer and political newcomer whose first time in the political arena is this midterm cycle, is running to unseat Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., in November.

As Election Day creeps closer, Cotton has gone on the offensive against her, attacking an apparent flip-flop in her position on Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the immigration enforcement agency under the Department of Homeland Security that became a political lightning rod in Congress earlier this year.
DEM REP SETH MOULTON SAYS PARTY HAS NO IMMIGRATION PLAN, IS ONLY ‘OPPOSITION TO TRUMP’
Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents walk a detainee out of the Ventura County Government Center in Ventura, Calif., on July 27, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)

Shoffner, during an appearance in June at the Immigrant Heritage Month Business Expo in Springdale, Ark., was asked whether she would defund ICE — a position several Democrats running for office have taken this cycle, including progressives Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota.

"I would vote to defund ICE as it exists right now," Shoffner said. "Immigration and Customs Enforcement was created not that long ago, and it no longer serves the purpose it was originally created for."

"I would not spend one more dime on ICE, because — not just because of the human dignity issue — but also the fact that it is now the largest law enforcement agency in the country," she continued. "It has 10 times the budget of the organization that fights child sex trafficking."
GOP ADVANCES ICE FUNDING PACKAGE AFTER FORCING TRUMP'S CONTROVERSIAL $2B FUND INTO RETREAT

ICE became a political third rail earlier this year after fatal shootings in Minnesota and was at the center of the longest government shutdown in history, when Senate Democrats refused to fund the agency absent stringent reforms.
That prompted Senate Republicans to front-load $70 billion in funding for ICE and Border Patrol earlier this year.
Cotton’s campaign cut Shoffner's comments into attack ads and accused her of donating to former Vice President Kamala Harris 25 times, which prompted Shoffner to further define her position.
In a Facebook post from Tuesday in which Cotton was asked by a voter about Shoffner’s ICE position, she jumped into the comment section to argue, "I don’t want to defund ICE, I want to reform it."
‘ABOLISH ICE’ DEMOCRAT FREEZES IN LIVE INTERVIEW WHEN ASKED WHO SHOULD ENFORCE IMMIGRATION LAWS

Sens. John Barrasso of Wyoming, Tom Cotton of Arkansas, Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia and James Lankford of Oklahoma attend a news conference following Senate Republican policy luncheons at the U.S. Capitol on June 23, 2026. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"My opponent wants to defund ICE, just like Democrat socialists Alexandra Ocasio-Cortez and Abdul El-Sayed," Cotton told Fox News Digital. "Doing so would protect criminals from deportation, like the illegal alien gang member who was arrested in Carroll County just days ago. Defunding ICE would make Arkansas more dangerous."
Shoffner’s bid to unseat Cotton, who is running for a third term in the upper chamber, is one of the tougher battles during this midterm cycle for Democrats.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Arkansas hasn’t sent a Democrat to the Senate since former Sen. Mark Pryor, who Cotton defeated in 2014. Shoffner also doesn’t have the backing of the Democratic establishment, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., in Washington, D.C.

Shoffner has put distance between herself and Schumer, too, telling Politico in March that while Democrats had found the issue of affordability to be a "magic bullet" at the national level, Arkansans were going to give Schumer "the side eye, because what does he know about affordability?"
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Three new companies face Josh Hawley's investigation into AI surveillance and vehicle tracking
summary: Josh Hawley expands his AI surveillance probe beyond Flock Safety to three more companies building massive camera networks that track Americans.
story: 'Outnumbered' debates privacy concerns surrounding Flock surveillance cameras after allegations of misuse by law enforcement, while weighing the technology’s role in solving crimes, locating missing people and protecting public safety.

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., is expanding his investigation into alleged privacy violations from Flock Safety cameras to three additional companies amid concerns about the handling of images and data generated by AI-backed surveillance cameras.
Hawley put Motorola Solutions Inc., Verkada Inc. and Axon Enterprise Inc. on notice in a series of letters that the lawmaker sent on Wednesday.

"On August 26th, I wrote to your competitor Flock Safety to express my concerns regarding the size and pervasiveness of its network and demanding answers as to reports of abuse and costly errors from its technology," Hawley’s letter to the three companies reads. "However, Flock does not stand alone in this industry; you and others are building large camera networks, assisted by artificial intelligence, that intrude on the privacy of all Americans."
HAWLEY RIPS FLOCK’S SPRAWLING SURVEILLANCE WEB AS TEXAS CITIES CUT CAMERAS OVER PRIVACY AND DATA FEARS
Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., talks with reporters in the U.S. Capitol during votes related to the government shutdown on Thursday, Oct. 16, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

Hawley, who serves as chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee's Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism, has been vocal about his concerns that Flock Safety cameras undermine personal privacy with an AI-powered system that tracks the movements of Americans.

"Americans do not surrender their privacy rights when they drive to work, drop their kids off at school or go to church," Hawley said in a post on X last week. "I’m investigating Flock cameras to determine WHO has access to hundreds of millions of Americans’ data - and what they’re doing with it."
POWERFUL CRIME-FIGHTING SURVEILLANCE GROWTH SPURS LAWMAKERS TO ISSUE WARNING: 'ORWELLIAN'

Hawley asked each of the companies to explain how broadly customers can search vehicle data, how long the company retains license plate information, how many confirmed cases of misuse have occurred since 2021 and what safeguards are in place to ensure law enforcement officers provide legitimate justifications before conducting searches.

A pigeon perches on a Flock Safety camera, mounted high on a traffic signal pole at the intersection of Chapman Avenue and Harbor Boulevard in Garden Grove, Calif. on Friday, Aug. 14, 2026. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

"We received the letter and have reached out to Senator Hawley’s office to discuss his requests," an Axon spokesperson said. "We welcome the opportunity to demonstrate our commitment to safety and responsible innovation."

A number of politicians have taken action against AI-powered cameras, with Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis ordering the removal of all license plate reader cameras from Florida state roads and Texas Gov. Greg Abbott ordering all state agencies to stop spending state money on Flock Safety cameras.
FLOCK SURVEILLANCE SPREADS ACROSS THE SOUTH AS RED-STATE LAWMAKERS SEEK TO AX '1984'-STYLE TRACKING TOOLS

Flock Safety cameras use artificial intelligence to automatically track and identify vehicles and license plates for local law enforcement use. Nationwide concern has grown about whether the AI-backed system should be allowed to track the movement of vehicles without a warrant or the consent of drivers.
About 120,000 Flock Safety cameras operate in every state except Alaska.
Last week, Hawley also sent a letter to Flock Safety, requesting similar information from the company.
In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for Flock Safety said the company would comply with the investigation.
FLOCK SAFETY CEO CALLS FOR NATIONAL 'COMPROMISE' AMID CAMERA SABOTAGE AND PUBLIC REVOLT
Texas Gov. Greg Abbott moved to cut off state-agency funding for Flock cameras as communities across the state reconsider their use of the technology. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

"We look forward to working with Senator Hawley and the Subcommittee to provide additional context about how our technology works, the safeguards built into our platform and how law enforcement agencies use Flock to solve crime and find missing people," Flock Safety spokesperson Paris Lewbel said.
INSIDE THE FAR-LEFT'S ANTI-DATA CENTER PUSH AND WHAT EXPERTS SAY IS DRIVING IT: 'PLAYBOOK WE'VE SEEN BEFORE'

The growing backlash against Flock cameras illustrates an unusual convergence: Republicans and far-left activists are arriving at the same target from sharply different ideological directions. While GOP lawmakers are focused on privacy, government overreach and protecting Americans from warrantless tracking, socialist and communist organizers have folded the cameras into a broader campaign against artificial intelligence, policing, immigration enforcement, the construction of data centers and the demonization of the United States as a "police state" and "AI surveillance state."

Over the past year, far-left organizations within a network funded by pro-China, Shanghai-based tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham have built vocal community campaigns against the Flock Safety cameras, while also targeting the construction of data centers. The GOP, including President Donald Trump and administration officials, have been leading voices of support for the continued construction of data centers.

In May, the Party for Socialism and Liberation’s Denver chapter partnered with Indivisible and the far-left Sunrise Movement and promoted a forum examining the "connections between mass surveillance and data centers and how BOTH only serve the needs of billionaires and not our communities."
MARXIST ORGANIZER LEADS CAMPAIGN AGAINST VIRGINIA AI DATA CENTER AS FOREIGN INFLUENCE CONCERNS MOUNT

By July 25, in Tucson, Ariz., the local Party for Socialism and Liberation chapter joined "deFLOCK Tucson" and the "No Desert Data Center Coalition" for an event called "It’s ALL Connected" at the "Global Justice Center" on E. 26th Street.
The promotional material asked what mass surveillance, data centers and electric power had in common. The answer: "IT’S ALL CONNECTED."

In a new report, "The Compute War at Home," commissioned by Consumer Action for a Strong Economy, the authors note that "money, media, organizing capacity and campaign objectives converge in the same ecosystem."

David Chung, organizing director at The People’s Forum, prepares for an anti-war demonstration in Union Square in New York City, left. Tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham attends The Red Party in New York City on Feb. 14, 2018, right. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News Digital; Mark Sagliocco/Getty Images)

"Issue pairings rarely multiply fourteen-fold in a matter of weeks without a catalyst, particularly when the surge begins immediately after organizers start promoting the connection," the report states.

Preston Mizell is a writer with Fox News Digital covering breaking news.

title: Rep Ralph Norman affirms that he'll 'support' ex-rival Sen Darline Graham in election
summary: Republican Rep. Ralph Norman affirmed that he will support former South Carolina special GOP U.S. Senate primary runoff rival Sen. Darline Graham in the general election.
story: Rep. Ralph Norman responds after being asked on Aug. 31 whether there is "a world where" he would "campaign for or support, even tacitly," Sen. Darline Graham. (Credit: CSPAN)
Rep. Ralph Norman, R-S.C., indicated in a Wednesday post on X that he would "support" Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., in South Carolina's U.S. Senate general election contest.

"As I said repeatedly on the campaign trail, my fight was never with other Republicans. It's with the socialist Democrats and the RINOs who enable them," Norman said in part of the post. "I respect the decision of South Carolina voters, and I congratulate Senator Darline Graham on winning the Republican nomination. I will support our Republican nominee in November because defeating the Democrats and protecting our conservative values must remain the priority."
South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster appointed Graham, the sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, to fill the vacancy following her brother's death in July.
Then in August, the new senator, who was backed by President Donald Trump, defeated Norman in the South Carolina special Republican U.S. Senate primary runoff.
TRUMP ENDORSEMENT BOOSTS SISTER OF LATE LINDSEY GRAHAM TO HISTORIC RUNOFF VICTORY
Rep. Ralph Norman, R-S.C., speaks to the media as he departs a House Republican conference meeting in the basement of the U.S. Capitol on Sept. 1, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Finn Gomez/Getty Images)
During remarks the day he lost the runoff last week, Norman had said he would "support" the senator the "best I can."
But earlier this week, someone asked Norman whether there is "a world where" he would "campaign for or support, even tacitly," Sen. Darline Graham.
THE PRIMARY IS OVER; NOW COME THE PRIMETIME MISTAKES
Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., speaks during a campaign event at the Green Boundary Club on Aug. 24, 2026, in Aiken, S.C. (Sean Rayford/Getty Images)
"She won the nomination," Norman replied. "What I disagree with, she got all of her money from Washington D.C. The liberal PACs, Lisa Murkowski supported her. That's concerning."
Fox News Digital reached out to Graham's campaign on Thursday but did not immediately hear back. Fox News Digital also reached out to Murkowski's office, which declined to provide comment.

President Donald Trump congratulates U.S. Sen. Darline Graham after she spoke during a campaign rally at Myrtle Beach Convention Center in Myrtle Beach, S.C., on Aug. 21, 2026. (SAUL LOEB / AFP via Getty Images)

Dr. Annie Andrews is the Democratic U.S. Senate nominee running against Graham in the general election.
Alex Nitzberg is a writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Musk picks his first GOP warriors as a 2026 money surge takes shape
summary: America PAC spent over $800,000 in 12 days backing Republicans, with Ken Paxton's Texas Senate race receiving the largest share of Elon Musk's cash.
story: Senators Elizabeth Warren and Bernie Sanders voice strong criticism regarding Elon Musk's achievement of trillionaire status following SpaceX's historic IPO. They argue for a wealth tax, while co-hosts emphasize Musk's role in creating thousands of new millionaires among his employees, including engineers and factory workers, suggesting he is being unfairly targeted as a 'boogeyman' by Democrats for political gain.

Elon Musk’s super PAC made its first major publicly disclosed burst of midterm spending, dumping significant amounts of cash over a very short period of time into races Republicans virtually must win to retain control of Congress.

Between Aug. 19 and Aug. 31, Musk’s America PAC reported just over $800,000 in expenditures supporting Republican candidates and opposing their Democratic rivals — an average of roughly $70,000 per day. By far the largest concentration of Musk’s spending was in the Texas Senate race, where America PAC spent nearly $248,000 supporting Paxton and opposing Talarico.

Republicans are heading into the midterms with a massive cash advantage, but are struggling to secure advantageous positions in even traditionally Republican states such as Alaska, Iowa, Texas and Ohio, according to Fox News’ Power Rankings. Musk opening his pocketbook for the GOP, an eventuality that was once in doubt given his prior split with the president, could provide Republicans with a much-needed lifeline as November approaches.
JOHNSON DOWNPLAYS GOP'S MIDTERM WOES AS DEMOCRATS EYE HOUSE TAKEOVER: 'I AM VERY BULLISH'
The bulk of the spending went toward "printing" expenses paid out to Storytellers Group, a political vendor that specializes in direct-mail work.
Over his 12-day expenditure period, Musk spent $123,000 opposing Talarico’s candidacy and about $125,000 supporting Paxton, according to a campaign finance filing released Wednesday.
RNC CHAIR SAYS TALARICO'S GOP CROSSOVER HOPES ARE A 'PIPE DREAM': 'NOBODY IS GOING TO FOLLOW HIM'
Billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk has begun supporting Republican candidates in the upcoming midterm elections. (BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/AFP via Getty Images)

The spending, while helpful to Republicans, gives Democrats a new angle of attack to use in the districts where Musk’s PAC is deploying resources. Musk has suffered from low favorability ratings among Americans, and his efforts with the Department of Government Efficiency, likewise, proved unpopular.

Democrats running in the competitive races where Musk is spending can now credibly tie their opponents to the billionaire. Talarico, for instance, has made running against billionaire interests a focal point of his campaign, a plank that increases in relevance now that Musk has waded into his race.
AFTER PLATNER IMPLOSION, MAINE DEMOCRATS RUSH TOWARD NEW SENATE NOMINEE DESPITE FRESH WARNING SIGNS

Left: Democratic Texas state Rep. James Talarico. Right: Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton. The two are running against each other for U.S. Senate.  (Brandon Bell/Getty Images; Nick Wagner/AP Photo)

Musk’s PAC also spent a considerable amount in Maine’s Senate race, deploying roughly $135,000 against Democratic nominee Troy Jackson and about $35,000 to assist incumbent GOP Sen. Susan Collins. Collins has worked to distance herself from the Trump administration and national Republicans as she seeks re-election in a left-leaning state, an effort Musk’s spending could complicate.
Other races Musk’s PAC spent in include the Senate races in Michigan, Ohio and New Hampshire as well as a handful of competitive House races in states like New York, Florida and Wisconsin.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

GOP donors, fundraisers and lawmakers are worried that their current cash advantage may not be enough to deliver victory in November. They worry that President Donald Trump may not deploy his $400 million political war chest aggressively enough.

title: 33 House Dems break with Jeffries as party fractures over Israel
summary: The House passed a bill to cut federal funds to colleges participating in boycotts of Israel, but Democrats argue it violates free speech rights.
story: Chad Pergram reports from Capitol Hill on the growing split within the Democratic Party over support for Israel.
The House of Representatives passed a bill aimed at blocking federal funds to colleges that boycott Israel, with the vast majority of Democrats voting against it.

All but 33 left-wing lawmakers voted to block the measure, which would "prohibit an institution that participates in a non-expressive commercial boycott of Israel" from getting government funding. It would also force universities that do get federal funds to affirm their students "are not unreasonably obstructed" from studying abroad in Israel.

The measure passed 237 to 169, with all but two Republicans voting in favor. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and his top deputies were among the 167 Democrats to vote "no" alongside Reps. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., and Warren Davidson, R-Ohio.
It comes as antisemitism continues to be a growing threat in the U.S. amid Israel's war in Gaza.
CHAOS ERUPTS AS HOUSE PASSES $1.15T DEFENSE BILL WITH ISRAEL PROVISION: 'STOP STOKING JEW HATRED'
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., spoke during a news conference at the U.S. Capitol on July 13, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)
Democrats have argued the bill is an infringement on the First Amendment, while Republicans hold it up as a way to ensure Jewish students feel safe at U.S. colleges and universities.
Republicans have seized on Democrats' divisions on the issue, which has coincided with a far-left insurgency plunging the party into civil war ahead of the midterms.
HOUSE DEMOCRATS FRACTURE BADLY OVER MASSIE AMENDMENT TO CUT $3.3B IN U.S. AID TO ISRAEL

Far-left Democrats, like the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), have attacked members of their own party who they view as not sufficiently critical of Israel. It's translated into some antisemitic incidents, such as a gay Jewish Democrat running for Congress in California getting run out of a pro-transgender rights march over his support for Israel's sovereignty.
Scott Wiener told CNN that people in the crowd made references to his "Israeli handlers" while berating him, a well-worn antisemitic trope.
Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., speaks with union activists about free speech on college campuses at the Capitol in Washington, May 23, 2024. (J. Scott Applewhite/AP Photo)
DEM RUNNING FOR PELOSI’S SEAT MOCKED AFTER ANTI-ISRAEL HECKLERS CHASE HIM FROM SF TRANS MARCH
Those divisions were present on Thursday morning as well, with Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., co-leading the legislation that his own senior Democratic leadership opposed.

Gottheimer said of the legislation in a statement, "The goal of the BDS movement is the destruction of the democratic State of Israel, America’s critical ally in the global fight against terror. BDS has no place on college campuses or anywhere in our country. At a time when our Jewish students are facing death threats, being physically assaulted, and blocked from going to class simply for who they are, we must do everything possible to ensure they can learn safely, speak freely, and get the education they deserve."
But progressives, including Rep. Jerry Nadler, D-N.Y., who said he otherwise opposes the boycott, divestment and sanctions (BDS) movement against Israel, called it an attack on the Constitution.

"The First Amendment right to free speech does not apply only to agreeable speech. No matter how much I may disagree with BDS, and find it strategically stupid and morally repugnant, I will always fight to protect Americans’ right to speech with which I disagree," Nadler said in a statement.

Meanwhile, House Rules Committee Chairwoman Virginia Foxx, R-N.C., said BDS policies at colleges created hostile environments by "marginalizing Jewish students." She said it was the government's duty to protect the equal rights of those students, who she argued were living in a hostile environment at schools with anti-Israel policies.
CAMPUS ANTISEMITISM EXTENDS BEYOND STUDENT PROTESTS AND INTO CLASSROOMS, ADL WARNS

Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., questions Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell during a hearing in the Rayburn House Office Building on Capitol Hill on June 24, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)
"They are discriminating against people of the Jewish faith," Foxx said. "Now is not the time for talk. It is the time for action."
Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., said during debate on the bill that it was Jewish students who were often leading BDS movements on college campuses.

"This is an attack on free speech and academic freedom, all in the name of defending a genocidal apartheid state," Tlaib said. "A vote for this bill is a betrayal of those promising young students...because they want to save lives, no matter their faith or ethnicity."

title: Powerful union leader backs Republican in key Senate showdown
summary: Sean O'Brien, one of the top union leaders in the country, backed Sen. Roger Marshall in the Kansas Senate race against Democrat Adam Hamilton.
story: Vice President JD Vance and some House Republicans are pushing union-friendly legislation, signaling a new era for the Republican Party.

FIRST ON FOX: One of the top union leaders in the country has waded into a key Senate contest, backing the Republican incumbent in a race that could determine the balance of power in the upper chamber.

Teamsters General President Sean O’Brien is backing Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., in his bid for re-election as Republicans look to solidify their grip in the upper chamber and push back against the headwinds that browbeat the party in power during a midterm election cycle.

"Sen. Marshall has proven time and time again that he is a friend of labor," O’Brien said in a statement first obtained by Fox News Digital. "As a member of the U.S. Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions, Sen. Marshall has been eager to partner with us on legislation that protects workers, even when it requires breaking rank with his own party."
EXCLUSIVE: TRUMP-BACKED CHALLENGER GAINS LABOR UNION SUPPORT IN KEY RACE FOR HOUSE CONTROL

Sean O'Brien, general president of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, speaks during a press conference outside the West Wing of the White House on Oct. 30, 2025, in Washington, D.C., flanked by Vice President JD Vance and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. (AFP via Getty Images)
"We look forward to continuing to work together with Sen. Marshall to fight for the rights of hardworking Americans," he continued.

O’Brien’s green light to Marshall comes as Teamsters Local 696, the Topeka, Kansas-based chapter of the Teamsters, also threw its support behind the lawmaker, who is seeking a second term in the Senate.

"We are proud to endorse the candidate in this race who continues to be a voice for the middle-class workers of our great state, and that candidate is Sen. Marshall," Local 696 President Mike Scribner said in a statement.
"Kansas Teamsters need someone in Washington who is willing to fight on their behalf," he continued. "Throughout his tenure, Sen. Marshall has shown that he is the person for the job."
O’Brien has morphed into a notable figure in the GOP after his appearance as one of the opening speakers at the Republican National Convention in 2024.
'LET'S BREW IT IN THE UNITED STATES': TEAMSTERS TARGET MODELO AND CORONA IN PUSH FOR MEXICAN BEER TARIFFS

He also formed a political alliance and friendship with one of President Donald Trump’s top allies, Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., and even backed Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s nomination to the job after nearly coming to blows with the Trump official two years prior.

It’s Marshall’s backing of pro-labor bills, like Hawley’s Faster Labor Contracts Act, and Sen. Ed Markey’s, D-Mass., Warehouse Worker Protection Act and his own Railway Safety Act that scored him the backing of the Teamsters. He also led the Overtime Wages Relief Act, which eliminated federal income tax on up to $10,000 of overtime wages for individuals and $20,000 for married filers as part of Trump's "one big, beautiful bill."

Marshall is running against Kansas Senate Democratic nominee Adam Hamilton, the lead pastor of the state’s largest Methodist megachurch. Kansas is a ruby-red stronghold, meaning national Republicans aren’t rushing to aid the incumbent in warding off Hamilton.
FOUR MONTHS TO MIDTERMS: 12 RACES THAT WILL DETERMINE THE SENATE MAJORITY
Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., wants to codify President Donald Trump's desire to cap credit card interest rates for a year. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)
Still, Hamilton has already proven a deft fundraiser, nearly matching Marshall’s war chest in a fraction of the time.
Hamilton has so far raised just north of $4.1 million, while Marshall has brought in just over $6.2 million in a race that Cook Political Report has rated as "likely Republican."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

But Hamilton will have to battle both a strong incumbent and history to have a chance at the seat. That’s because Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate in nearly a century. The last time was in the 1930s, when Kansans elected former Sen. George McGill. He only served one term before being ousted by a Republican.
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Maduro claims immunity, asks judge to dismiss drug-trafficking charges against him and his wife
summary: Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores argue sovereign immunity shields them from narco-terrorism and drug trafficking charges in a federal motion to dismiss.
story: Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas reports from Manhattan federal court as former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro appears for a hearing on narco-terrorism and drug-trafficking charges. Prosecutors allege Maduro led a drug-trafficking organization for over two decades. His attorneys are expected to argue he is immune from prosecution as a head of state and that his capture by U.S. Special Forces was unlawful. The Treasury Department authorized Venezuela to fund Maduro's legal defense.

Former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores asked a federal judge Wednesday to dismiss the drug trafficking charges against them, arguing, among other things, that the pair have sovereign immunity, according to court documents.

"No American court has ever presided over the criminal trial of a foreign leader who was recognized by their own country as the sitting head of state at the time the charges were brought. That is not an accident of history. It reflects a rule older than the common law: heads of state are exempt from the criminal process of any national court but their own," a memorandum Maduro's lawyers filed in support of their motion to dismiss read.

"That immunity flows not from goodwill that can be withdrawn on a whim, but from the perfect equality and absolute independence of sovereigns. Thus, this Court lacks jurisdiction with respect to Mr. Maduro, who is recognized by the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela as its head of state," the document continued.
MADURO ALLY DEPORTED TO US OVER ALLEGED BILLION-DOLLAR CORRUPTION SCHEME TIED TO OIL, FOOD PROGRAM
Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores were captured by U.S. forces in Caracas earlier this year and extradited to New York to face federal charges.  (Juan Barreto/AFP via Getty Images)

In January 2026, the United States Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York unsealed a fourth superseding indictment against Maduro and Flores. The indictment charged Maduro with narco-terrorism conspiracy, and both Flores and Maduro with cocaine importation conspiracy, possession of machine guns and destructive devices, and conspiracy to possess machine guns and destructive devices.

The indictment alleged that for decades, Maduro used his position — first as a deputy in Venezuela's National Assembly and then as the country's president — to conspire with narco-terrorists from some of the world's largest cartels to import cocaine into the United States.
Maduro's lawyers, however, claim that sovereign immunity prevents the U.S. from taking action against Maduro.

"The official character of these acts — such as issuing diplomatic passports, deploying the military, and announcing Venezuelan foreign policy — is apparent from the face of the Indictment. Because these actions were undertaken in his official capacity on behalf of a foreign sovereign, he may not be required to respond in this Court to the Indictment’s characterizations of his motives and intent in taking these actions," the document reads.
STATE DEPARTMENT ANNOUNCES 'TOTAL COMPLIANCE' FROM VENEZUELAN GOVERNMENT IN RELIEF EFFORTS AFTER MADURO ARREST

Captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro is escorted to the Daniel Patrick Manhattan United States Courthouse for an initial appearance to face U.S. federal charges, including narco-terrorism, conspiracy, drug trafficking and money laundering in New York City on Jan. 5, 2026. (Adam Gray/Reuters)
The U.S. government officially declared Maduro to be an illegitimate president in 2019 after Maduro declared victory in the disputed 2018 presidential election.
Maduro's lawyers also argue that the indictment violates his and Flores' due process, according to court documents.
The document asserts that Maduro "vehemently denies that he had anything to do with drug trafficking or intended to benefit anyone engaged in terrorism."

The motion to dismiss then argues that the charges against Maduro fail to establish that his alleged crimes took place in or were aimed at the United States, and therefore do not meet the standards of due process.
ARMY SOLDIER INVOLVED IN MADURO CAPTURE ARRESTED FOR ALLEGEDLY USING CLASSIFIED INTEL TO WIN $410K IN BETS

"The narcoterrorism statute, which was enacted in 2006 in connection with the reauthorization of the USA PATRIOT ACT, was intended to target foreign conduct. Recognizing that its power to police the rest of the world is not unlimited, Congress included a jurisdictional element that authorizes the use of the statute to prosecute foreign conduct under only five enumerated scenarios in which the foreign conduct is connected to the United States. Ignoring those parameters set by Congress, the Indictment fails — even by tracking the statutory language — to allege any basis for jurisdiction over the solely foreign conduct it alleges," the motion to dismiss reads.

The U.S. apprehended Maduro and Flores during a January military operation, titled Operation Absolute Resolve, in which U.S. forces captured the couple in Venezuela's capital of Caracas and extradited them back to the United States to be prosecuted in New York federal court.
TRUMP PICKS JAMES MCDONALD TO LEAD POWERFUL SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF NEW YORK AFTER JAY CLAYTON'S DEPARTURE

Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, are seen in handcuffs after landing at a Manhattan helipad, en route to a federal courthouse in Manhattan on Jan. 5, 2026, in New York City. (XNY/Star Max/GC Images via Getty Images)
Maduro is set to appear in court in November to begin oral arguments in support of his motion to dismiss.

title: 'Why would he do this to us?': One crucial Trump decision is hurting his base, Republicans warn
summary: Republican lawmakers warn President Donald Trump that his foreign beef import order is hurting loyal cattle ranchers ahead of the midterm elections.
story: ‘The Big Weekend Show’ panel discusses the potential economic fallout from waiving beef tariffs, including concerns that the move could undercut American cattlemen and hurt U.S. ranchers.
Republicans are warning President Donald Trump that his decision to flood supermarkets with foreign ground beef is hurting a key group in his base as the midterm elections near their climax.

Voters in beef-industry-heavy states, like South Dakota, Nebraska and Kansas, supported Trump in his bid for a second term. Now, lawmakers from those states say his decision to lift tariffs on hundreds of thousands of tons of foreign beef is putting the very people who elected him in a bind.

Sen. Mike Rounds, R-S.D., who is running for re-election, said his voters in South Dakota "love the president," and view him like a member of the family, but the beef import order feels like the administration "pulled the rug right out from underneath" them.
TRUMP WANTS CHEAPER BEEF. REPUBLICANS IN KEY RACES WARN HIS PLAN GOES TOO FAR
Cattle are herded at Lew Thompson's ranch on June 17, 2026, in Frio County, Texas. (San Antonio Express-News via Getty Images)
"They're hurt. I mean, they feel like they've been let down," Rounds said.

"Like, how could, you know, our friend, this guy that's as close to us as they've ever been to a president, how could he do this to them? I mean, that's the way they feel," he continued. "And that's the expression they're giving me is, ‘Why would he do this to us? Doesn't he understand ag?’"

Republicans are searching for an economic message to bring to voters as grocery bills, gas prices and other day-to-day necessities grow more expensive. Some argue that kneecapping ranchers and farmers, some of Trump’s most loyal supporters, in the name of affordability runs counter to that.

"I think people want an explanation," a House Republican granted anonymity to speak freely told Fox News Digital. "We want to be able to go to the ranchers, who are big Trump supporters, right, to be able to go to them and say, this administration is fighting for you."
THE UNEXPECTED FORCE KEEPING BEEF PRICES HIGH AND WHY THE PRESSURE COULD LAST FOR YEARS

Trump signed the order last week with the intent of flooding the market with 300,000 metric tons of imported ground beef, lowering costs for consumers thanks to a commitment that the product would be sold at 25% below current market prices over a 90-day span.

He also contended that it would allow ranchers to regrow the nation’s herds, which, thanks to a combination of drought and the invasive New World screwworm, has dwindled to historic lows not seen since the 1950s, according to data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA).

"I’m sympathetic to what he’s trying to get done," Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., told Keloland. "He’s trying to lower beef prices, which I think we’re all supportive of. I just don’t think this is the way to do it. And so, we have a lot of beef producers here in South Dakota; they produce the highest-quality beef in the world, and we’re trying to build our herds back up."

As the blowback mounts, the administration has acknowledged that ranchers are bearing the brunt of the blow. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer huddled privately with House Republicans on Wednesday afternoon, when several lawmakers pressed him on the subject of Trump’s beef imports.
NEBRASKA RANCHERS STRUGGLE TO RECOVER FROM HISTORIC WILDFIRES AS DROUGHT WORSENS CRISIS
President Donald Trump in the Oval Office of the White House on Aug. 31, 2026. (Annabelle Gordon/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Sources inside the room told Fox News Digital that Greer acknowledged ranchers were frustrated but maintained the import strategy was temporary. He argued it was the administration’s way of easing high prices on the market in the short term, the sources said.
But multiple House GOP lawmakers still said they were concerned as they exited the meeting.

"This is not just a one-year issue on the affordability of beef. We’ve got to make sure that we’ve got a Made-in-America-first beef program. That means standing with our cattlemen on that," Rep. Zach Nunn, R-Iowa, told Fox News Digital. "We’ve said the same thing to [Greer] in there."
Nunn, who is a top target for Democrats in November, said he planned to raise the issue again during dinner with Trump at the White House on Wednesday evening.

Rep. Troy Downing, R-Mont., pointed out that it was a relatively small amount of beef for just a 90-day period but said he was worried about the timing as it overlaps with the time of year farmers bring their cattle to market.

"If a rancher is expecting to get a price at market that suddenly drops out from underneath them, they’re faced with two things — they don’t have a stable market, so do I invest in heifers for next year? Or do I have to sell more calves to make up for that deficit for my operating costs? Which, neither one is helping rebuild the herd," Downing told Fox News Digital.
House Main Street Caucus Chairman Mike Flood, R-Neb., said he was opposed to a "tariff regime that undercuts American ranchers," but said Trump’s policies were helping in the "big picture."
Compounding people’s anxiety in the meeting was Trump’s trade war with Canada, which that House Republican said made northern-border-state GOP lawmakers "nervous."
Republican Study Committee Chairman August Pfluger, R-Texas, told Fox News Digital there would likely be "quite a few" follow-up meetings.
"It was absolutely outstanding, we had a tremendous amount of participation and people that were really excited to ask good questions," he said of the meeting in general.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
And Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said at an event in Iowa on Tuesday that the administration understood that "ranchers felt like that was a gut punch."

The White House argued that Trump "has done more for American agriculture than anyone" with trade deals, foreign market access expansion, lowering input costs, bolstering the farm safety net, doubling the death tax exemption, ending taxes on rural property loan interest, and creating rural opportunity zones."

"At the same time, he is delivering on his promise to consumers by reducing beef prices while allowing our American beef herd to grow," White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly told Fox News Digital. "The President will continue taking actions to support our great farmers while driving economic prosperity for all Americans."
Republican critics of the move are urging the administration to look at other methods to expand the nation’s cattle herds.

Several Republicans, led by Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., wrote to Rollins and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to lift Biden-era rules and ease federal guardrails to allow for more access to grazing land for cattle.

"The Federal government must remain laser-focused on partnering with the industry and state efforts for ranchers, expand grazing on public and private lands, and improve protein processing capacity," they wrote in a letter to the top Trump officials on Tuesday.
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: FIRST ON FOX: ‘No Kings’ protest network behind fight against AI data centers and Flock cameras
summary: Fox News Digital traces how pro-China socialist groups moved from anti-Trump, anti-Israel protests into technology messages that spread to conservatives and libertarians.
story: Rob Joyce, former cybersecurity director at the National Security Council, tells Fox News Digital the "influence actions are cognitive warfare" with unsuspecting Americans arguing "for the outcomes Beijing wants."

FIRST ON FOX: The same hard-left network behind "No Kings" and other protests is leading the battle against data centers and Flock surveillance cameras, according to a Fox News Digital investigation and a new report.

In growing protests from San Francisco to North Carolina, organizations and activists associated with the same ecosystem that rallied against President Donald Trump, Israel, Elon Musk, Tesla and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) over the last two years are now taking on data-center construction and license-plate readers.

The overlap includes organizations funded by pro-China, Shanghai-based tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham, whose sprawling nonprofit and media network has faced Congressional and federal scrutiny over its funding and foreign ties. Singham and the nonprofits he has funded have denied taking orders from any government or political party and haven’t been charged with any crimes.
INSIDE THE FAR-LEFT'S ANTI-DATA CENTER PUSH AND WHAT EXPERTS SAY IS DRIVING IT: 'PLAYBOOK WE'VE SEEN BEFORE'
Protesters rally against the use of Flock cameras on Friday, April 3, 2026, outside City Hall in Troy, N.Y. (Jim Franco/Times Union via Getty Images)

The findings are detailed in a new report, "The Compute War at Home," commissioned by Consumer Action for a Strong Economy, an Alexandria, Va., free-markets nonprofit that used social-media analysis by Arken Intelligence, a technology firm based in Washington, D.C., for parts of its study.
"The money, media, organizing capacity and campaign objectives converge in the same ecosystem," the report says.

Based on reporting over the past several years from street protests, Fox News Digital has identified the protest movement’s evolution across three phases. The new report chronicles a repeatable political model, in which activists first identify a local grievance, then connect it to a larger ideological narrative and package the argument through national media and activist infrastructure and carry it into new communities.

The first phase appeared in early January 2025 with Trump’s inauguration and the launch of "Tesla Takedown" demonstrations to protest Tesla founder Musk as he led efforts to cut waste in federal spending. It became the mobilization infrastructure built around "No Kings" and "Hands Off" anti-Trump protests, anti-Israel activism and related campaigns, supporting the Communist Party of Cuba, the Islamic Republic of Iran and Venezuelan communist strongman Nicholas Maduro.

Organizations from the Singham network – including the Party for Socialism and Liberation, CodePink, the People’s Forum, ANSWER Coalition and affiliated groups – appeared repeatedly across those movements, working with nonprofits more aligned with the Democratic Party, including Indivisible, a nonprofit network funded in part by billionaire Democratic megadonor George Soros. The organizations deny any wrongdoing as agents of alleged foreign influence and say they are addressing legitimate community grievances.
AGITATORS UNITED BY CHINESE MONEY, HATE FOR AMERICA TARGET DATA CENTERS, EXPERTS WARN
Medea Benjamin, co-founder of CodePink, holds a sign supporting Cuba at Miami International Airport on March 20, 2026, before a delegation travels to Cuba. (Eva Marie Uzcategui/AFP)

The second phase shifted that protest infrastructure toward American technological infrastructure. Over the past year, CodePink developed a national campaign against data centers, while the campaign took root among the approximately 70 chapters of the Party for Socialism and Liberation with near-identical messaging and strategies. Liberation News, which describes itself as the newspaper of the Party for Socialism and Liberation, nationalized local victories and promoted moratoria, bans and project cancellations. Media outlets, like BreathThrough News, from the Singham network provided additional amplification.

The third phase involved an ideological crossover in which Flock cameras have now become a bridge between local privacy and policing concerns and the national fight over artificial intelligence, cloud systems, energy and data centers.

The report doesn’t claim that every opponent of Flock cameras or data centers is connected to the activist network. It notes that opposition to Flock has become genuinely bipartisan, with legitimate concerns about privacy, data retention, misuse and poorly written government contracts. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis recently ordered license-plate readers removed from state highways, while Texas has also moved to pull back from the technology, and Republican Sen. Josh Hawley has launched an investigation into Flock cameras over surveillance concerns.
But the report credits the left-wing organizers with fusing the two issues into a one-two punch that has caught on with a broad coalition.

According to the Arken Intelligence analysis, posts mentioning both Flock and data centers increased from 639 posts in the 10 weeks before a spike in organizing on May 19 led to 9,009 posts over the next 10 weeks, a 14.1-fold increase.
Among posts for which a political affiliation could be classified, the report said, 81% came from right-wing, conservative or libertarian accounts.

"Issue pairings rarely multiply fourteen-fold in a matter of weeks without a catalyst, particularly when the surge begins immediately after organizers start promoting the connection," the report states.

"These influence actions are cognitive warfare. Foreign actors don't need Americans to become pro-China," Rob Joyce, former director of cybersecurity at the National Security Agency, told Fox News Digital. "They need Americans to argue for the outcomes Beijing wants. And a free society that can't build the power and govern the advanced technology is going to wind up renting it from the adversary, read the PRC, that doesn't share its own values. And that scares me as an American."
DOJ LAUNCHES GRAND JURY PROBE INTO MARXIST MOGUL NEVILLE ROY SINGHAM'S FUNDING OF LEFTIST GROUPS
Protestors hold up "Stop data centers" signs, on the day of U.S. President Donald Trump's speech at the General Motors Proving Ground, in Milford, Mich., U.S. July 27, 2026. (Carlos Osorio/Reuters)

The report identifies at least a year of coordination among far-left activists in the Singham network, deliberately linking the issues through propaganda media outlets and activist networks funded and supported by Singham.

Late last September, BreakThrough News laid the groundwork, publishing an article that described Flock as "America’s authoritarian tracking infrastructure." Soon after, People’s Dispatch, now merged into the BreakThrough News operations, covered a Denver campaign against data centers the next month, using a photograph from the Party for Socialism and Liberation’s Denver chapter and quoting a local Party for Socialism and Liberation organizer.

By early May, the Party for Socialism and Liberation’s Denver chapter partnered with Indivisible and the far-left Sunrise Movement and promoted a forum examining the "connections between mass surveillance and data centers and how BOTH only serve the needs of billionaires and not our communities."
PROBE INTO 'SUBVERSIVE' ANTI-AI SINGHAM NETWORK IS 'ENORMOUS,' FORMER TREASURY ADVISOR SAYS

David Chung, organizing director at The People’s Forum, prepares for an anti-war demonstration in Union Square in New York City, left. Tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham attends The Red Party in New York City on Feb. 14, 2018, right. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News Digital; Mark Sagliocco/Getty Images)

Days later, on May 19, when the convergence of issues went public, the local Denver chapter of the Party for Socialism and Liberation circulated a petition to urge the Denver city council to block the building of data centers, arguing, "FIGHTING BACK AGAINST DATA CENTERS MEANS FIGHTING FOR SOCIALISM!" It also posted photos opposing Flock cameras.

On July 11, in Charlotte, N.C., the Party for Socialism and Liberation’s local chapter published an anti-Flock post centered on "AI mass surveillance" and police "brutality," then directed readers to sign a North Carolina petition opposing data-center construction on a dedicated website, nodatacentersnc.com, anonymously purchased the month earlier on June 19, according to online records.

By July 25, in Tucson, Ariz., the local Party for Socialism and Liberation chapter joined "deFLOCK Tucson" and the "No Desert Data Center Coalition" for an event called "It’s ALL Connected" at the "Global Justice Center" on E. 26th Street.
The promotional material asked what mass surveillance, data centers and electric power had in common. The answer: "IT’S ALL CONNECTED."

The report says the campaigns combine concerns over water, electricity rates, land use, noise, health, immigration enforcement, policing and artificial intelligence. Those concerns can be legitimate, the report notes, but organizers can also use them to make the broader infrastructure supporting American computing appear inherently dangerous or illegitimate.

In July, CodePink’s Detroit chapter published a description of data centers as the physical infrastructure of mass surveillance, linking them to OpenAI, Palantir Technologies, military contractors and ICE, crafting a narrative around the argument that the AI data center industry "creates harm and destruction."

CodePink has dedicated a website page to a new campaign, "DATA CENTERS AND THE WAR ECONOMY," describing data centers as products and instruments of war and warning that projects "must be halted wherever they are." Its action page calls on activists to build a joint struggle against data centers and the "war economy."
TEXAS GOV. GREG ABBOTT MOVES TO CUT STATE FUNDING FOR AI-POWERED FLOCK CAMERAS AMID PRIVACY CONCERNS

Flock cameras provide a particularly effective local "entry grievances," according to the report. A dispute over a police contract, a license-plate reader or a single alleged misuse can be expanded into a broader argument about databases, artificial intelligence, cloud systems and data centers.
"Flock gives that abstraction a visible local target," the report states, allowing organizers to portray "a much larger infrastructure buildout" as threatening.

Flock’s actual computing footprint is small, according to company officials. According to Rahul Sidhu, chief strategy officer at Flock, the company uses less than 0.1% of the capacity of a single data center. But the report argues that Flock’s political value is far greater than its computational footprint because it gives the "surveillance state" argument a concrete and emotionally potent target.

Ultimately, the causes have converged, say experts, with Republican politicians joining the chorus of criticism by pro-China communists in recent days against data centers and Flock cameras. As the Party for Socialism and Liberation continued to rail against "AI mass surveillance," DeSantis this week opposed the rise of an "AI digital surveillance state."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The renewed scrutiny on the Singham network’s alleged influence operations on local communities emerges as it faces serious investigation by Congress and federal investigators. The Senate Judiciary Committee previously asked the Justice Department and FBI to assess whether CodePink and the People’s Forum should register under the Foreign Agents Registration Act, called FARA.

The House Oversight Committee has sought records concerning Singham’s funding relationships, while the House Ways and Means Committee recently sent subpoenas to BreakThrough News, Tricontinental and the People’s Forum, which have refused to supply documents, saying they are the targets of a "witch hunt."

As Fox News Digital first reported in late June, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York launched a grand jury investigation earlier this year that is examining possible money laundering, wire fraud and bank fraud violations by Singham and the network of nonprofits he funded.

Asra Nomani is senior editor of investigations at Fox News Digital. She is a former reporter at the Wall Street Journal, where she covered stories related to money, politics and society. She is the author of "Woke Army: The Left-Green Alliance That Is Undermining America’s Freedom." She can be reached at asra.nomani@fox.com and on X at @asranomani.

title: 2028 Dem hopeful's longtime ally exposed for deep ties to CCP officials: 'Good friends'
summary: Rep. Ro Khanna's, D-Calif. former senior advisor on foreign trade and economic development could be liability to a potential 2028 campaign due to his ties to CCP officials.
story: Swalwell sits on the House Intelligence Committee.

FIRST ON FOX: Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., has been floated as a potential 2028 Democratic contender for president, but his longtime ally and former senior advisor on foreign trade and economic development could be a liability due to his deep ties to Chinese Communist Party officials, a Fox News Digital investigation found.

Henry Yin is a longtime California businessman and political operative who Khanna has praised for his "leadership" and has called one of his "good friends" on Facebook. He was born in China, raised in Taiwan and then moved to the United States, where he has lived for several decades.

However, while living in California, Yin has been a major player helping China get a foothold in California over the last several decades through multiple roles, including serving as a member of the California Commission for Economic Development and founding a consulting firm that included multiple corporate clients with ties to Chinese Communist Party officials.

A 2011 profile piece revealed that Yin "made his fortune selling used computer equipment to China" and had "done business in China for more than a quarter-century." The profile piece went on to say Yin has "good connections and a sense of [China's] business climate" and was "leading city trade delegations to China, which have contributed to several Chinese firms — most recently software company Trunkbow International — setting up offices in the city and helping city businessmen get a foothold in China."
SWALWELL RESIGNATION COLLIDES WITH CHINA-LINKED SCANDAL AS CRITICS DEMAND FILE RELEASE

Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., joins fellow Democrats during a press conference on border negotiations as a deadline to avert a partial government shutdown approaches at the U.S. Capitol in Washington on Jan. 18, 2024. (Leah Millis/Reuters)

"Henry has some sort of special skill-building relationships," one businessman said in the profile piece, praising Yin. "There’s a lot more government involvement in China, and you need relationships with local government officials."

In addition to his consulting business and several overseas trips to China, Yin has allegedly attended at least 10 events hosted by United Front groups, including the All-China Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese (ACFROC), according to China expert Jackie Deal, the president of Long Term Strategy Group, a defense research firm. Fox News Digital has extensively reported on the CCP's United Front and the threat it poses to U.S. institutions as the CCP gains influence in the United States.

In a Sept. 2019 Facebook post, Khanna announced that Yin, who was first appointed to the California Commission for Economic Development in 2010 by then- Republican Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger and later reappointed to the position in 2015 by the succeeding Democratic Gov. Jerry Brown, would "serve as my Senior Advisor on Foreign Trade and Economic Development."

"We discussed the importance of improving the US China relationship to cooperate on issues of climate change and medical research while protecting intellectual property and opening access to markets," Khanna continued. "I was particularly touched that Henry and the group had a birthday cake for me. It was wonderful celebrating with them!"
A few months later, in December of the same year, Khanna posted about Yin on Facebook again, writing, "Thank you Henry Yin for your leadership!"

That same month, Yin invited Khanna to be his "honorable guest" for an event titled, "S.V. U.S.-China Trading Partners Concerned Group Dinner Meeting Agenda," which was sponsored by Yin's consulting firm, USA-China-Link. A review of the event's presentations showed the attendees were slated to talk about an array of topics, including China investments, technology and business asset management, among other topics. Khanna was slated to discuss intellectual property.
ELITE US COLLEGES LINKED TO CHINESE SURVEILLANCE LABS DRIVING UYGHUR ‘GENOCIDE,’ STUDY WARNS

Chinese President Xi Jinping reviews the honor guard during the welcome ceremony for Bahrain's King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa at the Great Hall of the People on May 31, 2024, in Beijing, China. (Tingshu Wang/Pool/Getty Images)

In Feb. 2020, Khanna posted another photo of himself having dinner with Yin, who he referred to as one of his "good friends." In the post, Khanna decried that "Chinese Americans are feeling they are being stereotyped as the symbols for the coronavirus."
"This is a time to embrace our Chinese American neighbors and friends and continue to frequent Chinese-American stores, restaurants and shopping centers."

On Yin's LinkedIn profile, which still includes the senior advisor title with Khanna's office, he includes over a dozen slides detailing his consulting business, USA-China-Link, and showcasing his business acumen in China, which was featured in several profile pieces in Chinese state media. One of the slides says his firm "specialized in high-tech and green tech" and helped China do business in California and vice versa. Other slides show a list of his Chinese clients and a slide that called him an "Official Commerce Rep in US for the Province of Fujian, China."

Another slide shows a photo of Yin at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing in 2009 for the China National Day Banquet, where he calls himself a "VIP" in the caption. According to reports on the event, the banquet included several senior-level CCP officials in attendance, including then-Chinese President Hu Jintao and his successor Xi Jinping, the former third-ranking member of the CCP's Politburo Standing Committee, Wen Jiabao, among other top officials.

A spokesperson for Khanna, who is a member of the House Select Committee on the CCP, told Fox News Digital earlier this year that "Henry Yin has never been employed by Rep. Khanna" and "he doesn’t serve in any role in his office or campaign." When asked Wednesday whether his office stands by the quote, Khanna's office did not immediately respond. Despite the previous denial, Khanna and Yin were pictured sitting beside each other earlier this year at an event.

In Feb. 2026, Khanna posted a photo showing him sitting beside Yin at a political action committee meeting in Sunnyvale, California. Khanna wrote he was "honored to be back in the district, hearing directly from Chinese American community leaders."

Yin has made several trips abroad to China over the last decade, including a July trip where he led a delegation to Guangzhou to meet with Zhu Xiaojun, the Department of Commerce of Guangdong Province's deputy director, which is a CCP-controlled position. A Chinese report on the trip said the two sides collaborated on two-way trade between California and the Guangdong province. Two months before the event, Yin attended the 2026 China-California Economic and Trade Forum, which was hosted by the Chinese Consulate in Los Angeles and included multiple CCP officials in attendance.

He also accompanied California Gov. Gavin Newsom in late 2023 for a delegation, where he served as an advisor, according to another Chinese media report. During the trip, Newsom would meet with top CCP officials, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Wang Yi, who has been a CCP member since 1981 and is currently serving as a "Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, and Minister of Foreign Affairs." Newsom also met with Han Zheng, China's vice president.

A Fox News Digital review of Yin's Facebook account also unearthed other China trips he made, including Chinese delegations he has helped host in California. In 2014, Yin signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) between the California Green Tech Center and China Venture Capital Association, which appeared to be one of his firm's clients. Other posts show multiple China visits, including the 2015 "China South Asia Expo," which featured a speech from the now-former Chinese Vice President Li Yuanchao. A 2019 post highlights another China trip he took, which he called "fruitful" and included over a dozen photos of Chinese officials he met with. One of the photos included the names of Chinese and American companies where he was facilitating trade projects.

In this photo taken Wednesday, Oct. 25, 2023 and released by the Office of the Governor of California, California Gov. Gavin Newsom, left, meets with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. (Office of the Governor of California via AP)
ELITE US COLLEGES LINKED TO CHINESE SURVEILLANCE LABS DRIVING UYGHUR ‘GENOCIDE,’ STUDY WARNS

A Fox News Digital investigation also unearthed a 2013 photo that appears to show Christine "Fang Fang" Fang — the Chinese spy at the center of the scandal involving disgraced former Rep. Eric Swalwell — alongside key political figures. Posing together at a public gathering, Fang stood behind then-Chinese Consul General to San Francisco Gao Zhansheng and top leaders from the Asian Pacific Islander American Public Affairs Association (APAPA), including Yin.

A recently declassified FBI report on Swalwell's ties to Fang Fang revealed that a "prominent businessman in the Bay Area" tied to APAPA introduced Swalwell to Fang Fang. While Fox News Digital could not confirm whether the redacted section of the FBI report was referring to Yin, or potentially his brother, C.C., who founded APAPA and opened up several McDonald's franchises, Axios previously quoted Yin saying that Fang Fang was "very active" with the APAPA Bay Area chapter and remembered seeing her at several events.

The photo was originally shared on Facebook in February 2013 by the late Don Sun, a prominent California civic leader and tech executive who passed away in 2024. In the photo caption, Sun wrote that the Yin family and APAPA had thrown a farewell dinner for the Chinese consul at San Francisco’s Embarcadero Center. Sun said the photo depicts the consul and "all my friends at APAPA."
UNEARTHED PHOTO OF SWALWELL MEETING WITH TOP CCP OFFICIAL RAISES ALARM BELLS: 'VERY DISTURBING'
Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) sits at a town hall event on February 20, 2026, in Stanford, California. The town hall focused on taxing billionaires and the future of AI. (Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images)

An APAPA spokesperson confirmed that Yin is a current member of the group's board. The spokesperson wrote in an emailed statement earlier this year that the photo "appears to reflect a private gathering and does not represent APAPA programming, partnerships, or operations." They emphasized that attendance by individual members of APAPA at events "does not reflect organizational positions, affiliations, or activities beyond that context."

"Public officials should strongly scrutinize any APAPA efforts that align with CCP objectives, including the CCP influence operations to prevent data center construction across America," Michael Lucci, the CEO of State Armor, a nonprofit countering CCP threats, told the New York Post.

"APAPA does not have documentation to substantiate the characterization in Mr. Sun’s post that the dinner was ‘co-hosted’ by APAPA, and we cannot validate third party descriptions of the event based on a photo and a social media caption," the spokesperson said, adding, "Individuals may attend events in a personal capacity, and such attendance should not be construed as an organizational activity or endorsement."

The spokesperson also noted that "APAPA has no records indicating that he [Yin] has served as a senior advisor to Rep. Khanna" despite an APAPA press release from January 2022 announcing Yin joining the group's national governing board and states that he "has served as Senior Advisor to U.S. Representative Ro Khanna, who represents the South Bay Area."

Democratic Rep. Ro Khanna of California speaks with Fox News Digital ahead of a rally that he organized which included Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner, in Bar Harbor, Maine on June 5, 2026. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)

Pressed by Fox News Digital on this, the APAPA spokesperson said, "The current APAPA headquarters leadership and team had no knowledge of, and do not maintain any records confirming, Mr. Henry Yin serving as a senior advisor to Rep. Khanna. APAPA does not oversee, verify, or maintain records related to an individual’s outside titles or roles with public officials."

They added that "With respect to historical references appearing on legacy APAPA web pages or posts, APAPA is in the process of reviewing and removing outdated or inaccurate content that does not reflect current leadership, governance, or verified records." They added that "questions regarding any past or current status with Rep. Khanna’s office should be directed to that office or to Mr. Yin directly."

title: GOP mail-in voting proposal could impact millions of Americans ahead of midterms
summary: President Donald Trump's allies unveil a bill requiring mail-in ballots be received by Election Day, citing Florida's system as proof it works.
story: House GOP Rep. Laurel Lee spoke with Fox News Digital about her new legislative proposal that mail-in ballots have to be received by the time polls close on Election Day.

FIRST ON FOX: The nationwide battle over how and when Americans can vote has hit Capitol Hill, with two allies of President Donald Trump unveiling a new proposal they say will help restore confidence in U.S. elections.

Rep. Laurel Lee, R-Fla., plans to introduce legislation on Thursday mandating that absentee and mail-in ballots are received by the relevant officials by the end of the day on Election Day. A corresponding bill is being led in the Senate by Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla.

"This is something that we've done in Florida for many years, and it's a really effective way of making sure that elections stay organized and that we have timely election results," Lee told Fox News Digital.
SUPREME COURT RULES ON MAIL-IN BALLOTS RECEIVED AFTER ELECTION DAY
People cast their ballots during early voting on Oct. 25, 2025, in New York. (Olga Fedorova/AP)
Lee is Florida's former top elections official, having served as its secretary of state from 2019 until May 2022.

"Florida is proof-positive that this works, that it does not deny any voter the right to vote. Our job as elected officials or as elections officials throughout the states is just to make sure that voters know the deadlines, that they know the rules and tell them your ballot has to be received," Lee said. "They can do that just as easy as they can get it postmarked by Election Day."
TRUMP SCORES SUPREME COURT WIN ON MAIL-IN VOTING RESTRICTIONS BEFORE MIDTERMS
It follows an executive order Trump issued in March 2025 essentially setting an Election Day deadline for when mail-in ballots can be received.
If passed, the legislation could have a significant impact on millions of Americans, nearly a third of whom vote by mail.
President Donald Trump displays a signed executive order in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday, March 31, 2026. (Aaron Schwartz/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION FROM RESTRICTING MAIL-IN BALLOTS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

However, the topic of mail-in ballots has been a political lightning rod that's divided the GOP. Republicans in states where voting by mail is popular have expressed concern about changing the current system ahead of November.
But Lee argued her bill does not curb people's ability to vote by mail.
REPUBLICAN SAYS TRUMP'S TOP ELECTION PRIORITY 'DEAD' IN SENATE AS GOP FRACTURES AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

"One thing that's important to understand about this bill is that it doesn't limit voting by mail. It simply says that for states who allow mail voting, ballots must be received by Election Day," she said. "So it still keeps all of those options that states have chosen to implement on the table for them. It just creates a different deadline."

Moody told Fox News Digital of the bill, "The Ballots by Election Day Act is a simple fix to rebuild trust in elections. The fact that some states allow ballots to pour in for days after an election is absurd.  Passing our Ballots by Election Day Act would deliver results before bed."
Meanwhile, a separate Trump order making significant changes to the mail-in voting system is currently at the center of a dramatic legal battle between the White House and over 20 states.

That order would create new hurdles for the U.S. Postal Service and other agencies to verify proof of citizenship before delivering ballots, as well as mandate the use of specific stationery denoting federal election mail.

Supporters of the rule have argued it's key to enhancing voter confidence in elections, while opponents have said it would do the opposite by sowing chaos in the current system.
